=== NOTES 5:13 | Networks and the Internet – Lan/wan, Protocols, Ip, Dns, Web Technologies
## SUB 0 | Web Technologies – Browsers, Search Engines, HTML and Web Terms
[13:0:0] # Browser vs search engine (most-asked angle)
[13:0:1] TABLE head: Name | What it is
  [13:0:1.0] Chrome | Web browser by Google (2008) – not a search engine
  [13:0:1.1] Internet Explorer (now Edge), Firefox, Opera, Vivaldi, Safari | Web browsers
  [13:0:1.2] Yahoo | Search engine / web portal – not a browser
  [13:0:1.3] Bing | Search engine of Microsoft, launched 2009 (not Ming, Buzz)
  [13:0:1.4] Baidu | Chinese search engine
  [13:0:1.5] DuckDuckGo | Search engine that does not track or collect user information
  [13:0:1.6] Altavista | Early search engine
  [13:0:1.7] Kurrently | Real-time social-media search engine
  [13:0:1.8] Orkut | Closed social networking site (Google, shut 2014) – not a search engine
  [13:0:1.9] Google Apps | Office/productivity suite – not a web browser
  [13:0:1.10] Snapdeal | E-commerce company – not a means of communication (Darknet, Internet, Bluetooth are)
[13:0:2] - **Web browser:** software that requests and **displays web pages** (not a website, interpreter or OS); browsers use HTTP/HTTPS.
[13:0:3] - **Search engine:** indexes web pages so they can be found; **Yahoo, Google, MSN** are internet sites (portals).
[13:0:4] - **Web crawler** = **web spider** (spiderbot): bot that scans the Web for search-engine indexing.
[13:0:5] - **Home page:** the **first page** a browser shows on opening a website.
[13:0:6] - **URL (Uniform Resource Locator):** the site address typed to view pages – protocol (`https://`) → domain name → path to the file.
[13:0:7] - **Cookie:** a **small piece of data** a website sends and the **browser stores** while the user browses (not a thumbnail or worm).
[13:0:8] - **Webmercial:** a commercial message (advertisement) on the Web.
[13:0:9] # Languages of the Web
[13:0:10] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [13:0:10.0] HTML | HyperText Markup Language – the language of the WWW; used to display web pages in a browser (not HTTP, which is a protocol)
  [13:0:10.1] Web server | Keeps information in web pages whose text is marked with HTML tags and serves them on request
  [13:0:10.2] `<em>` tag | Marks emphasised text, i.e. indicates the importance/stress of the text (shown in italics); not a list tag or font-size tag
  [13:0:10.3] PHP | Hypertext Preprocessor – popular server-side scripting language for dynamic, data-driven web apps
  [13:0:10.4] JSP | Java Server Pages – dynamic web pages; released 1999 by Sun Microsystems
  [13:0:10.5] Front-end core | HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript
  [13:0:10.6] OCEN | Open Credit Enablement Network – democratises lending so small borrowers get good credit terms
[13:0:11] - **W3C = World Wide Web Consortium:** main international **web standards body**, founded **1994** by **Tim Berners-Lee**; keeps pages working alike across browsers.
[13:0:12] # Web 1.0 → 2.0 → 3.0
[13:0:13] TABLE head: Phase | Nature | User role
  [13:0:13.0] Web 1.0 (1990s) | Static HTML pages | Read-only
  [13:0:13.1] Web 2.0 (mid-2000s–) | Interactive, social, user-generated content; Big Tech holds data | Read-write
  [13:0:13.2] Web 3.0 | Decentralised (blockchain), semantic/AI web | Read-write-own
[13:0:14] - **Web 3.0 (UPSC 2022, all three correct):** people **control their own data**; **blockchain-based social networks** possible; **operated by users collectively** (DAOs) rather than a corporation.
[13:0:15] # Layers of the Web
[13:0:16] TABLE head: Layer | Share | Features
  [13:0:16.0] Surface (clear) web | ~4-5% | Indexed by search engines
  [13:0:16.1] Deep web | ~90-95% | Not indexed – inboxes, net banking, intranets; not always harmful
  [13:0:16.2] Dark web | Small hidden part of the deep web | Needs Tor / I2P; anonymous; linked with illegal markets
[13:0:17] > ⚠ Trap: Yahoo/Bing/Baidu = search engines; Chrome/Opera/Vivaldi = browsers; Orkut = social network; Google Apps = not a browser.
[13:0:18] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 5 p.63-66 (Web 1.0-3.0, HTML, UPSC 2022, browsers vs search engines); app notes 5:13 sub 7; general knowledge (PHP, JSP, `<em>`, webmercial, Kurrently)
## SUB 1 | Modem, Network Devices, Servers and the OSI Model
[13:1:0] # Modem (asked ~15 times)
[13:1:1] - **Modem = MOdulator-DEModulator:** converts **digital → analog** (modulation) and **analog → digital** (demodulation) – **both** ways.
[13:1:2] - **Job:** the **hardware unit that connects a home computer to the internet through a telephone line**; it **interfaces telephone lines and computer equipment** and lets computers **send and receive data worldwide**.
[13:1:3] - It is **hardware** – not software, an OS or a voltage stabiliser; it does not encrypt or check for viruses.
[13:1:4] - **Statement set (UPPCS 2009):** LCD = main use of liquid crystals ✓; modem connects a computer to a phone line ✓; NIO is at **Goa** (not Coimbatore) ✗; **70 Virginis** is a **star** (not a video system) ✗ → **only 1 and 2**.
[13:1:5] # Devices
[13:1:6] TABLE head: Device | Job | OSI layer
  [13:1:6.0] NIC (network card) | Connects a computer to the network; holds the MAC address | 1-2 (Physical/Data Link)
  [13:1:6.1] Hub | Broadcasts to all ports | 1 Physical
  [13:1:6.2] Repeater | Regenerates a weak signal to extend the cable | 1 Physical
  [13:1:6.3] Switch / Bridge | Forwards frames by MAC address | 2 Data Link
  [13:1:6.4] Router | Connects different networks; routes by IP | 3 Network
  [13:1:6.5] Firewall | Filters traffic by rules | 3-4 (and above)
  [13:1:6.6] Gateway | Joins networks using different protocols | up to 7 Application
  [13:1:6.7] Modem | Signal conversion | 1 Physical
[13:1:7] - **Physical → application order (TS 2021):** **NIC → switch/bridge → router → firewall → gateway** (D, B, A, E, C).
[13:1:8] - **Router, hub and switch are all connecting devices** (MPPSC 2014 asked "which is a connecting device?" – answer "all of these").
[13:1:9] # Servers
[13:1:10] - **Proxy server:** middleman that **forwards client requests to other servers**; it does **not** provide TCP/IP addresses (DHCP does).
[13:1:11] - **Server types:** file, print, application, web, mail, database, proxy servers. "**Network server**" is the generic name for a powerful central computer storing shared data/programs – the MPPSC 2021 key treats it as "not a (type of) server".
[13:1:12] - **Nodes:** all computers and printers on a network are its **nodes**.
[13:1:13] # OSI model – seven layers (top to bottom)
[13:1:14] TABLE head: Layer | Function | Protocols / devices
  [13:1:14.0] 7 Application | User services | HTTP, FTP, SMTP, DNS
  [13:1:14.1] 6 Presentation | Encryption, compression, formats (JPEG) | –
  [13:1:14.2] 5 Session | Opens and closes sessions | –
  [13:1:14.3] 4 Transport | End-to-end delivery | TCP, UDP
  [13:1:14.4] 3 Network | Routing; IP addresses (Internet layer of TCP/IP) | Router
  [13:1:14.5] 2 Data Link | Framing, MAC addresses, error detection; Ethernet, PPP | Switch, bridge, NIC
  [13:1:14.6] 1 Physical | Signals on the medium | Cables, hub, repeater, modem
[13:1:15] - **Data Link layer** lies **between the Physical and Network layers**; OSI model ratified **1984**.
[13:1:16] - **SMTP** = **Application layer**; IP addresses = **Network layer**.
[13:1:17] > ⚠ Trap: switch = Layer 2 (MAC), router = Layer 3 (IP); modem is a Physical-layer device, not Transport.
[13:1:18] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 5 p.28 (networking devices: routers, switches, modems), p.45 (dial-up modem); app notes 5:13 sub 2; testbook.com (MPPSC 2014 "Which of the following is a connecting device?" – All of these); general knowledge (OSI device order, NIO Goa, 70 Virginis)
## SUB 2 | Internet and the World Wide Web – Basics and History
[13:2:0] # Internet
[13:2:1] - **Internet = "a network of networks"**: global network of interconnected computers working on **TCP/IP**; the **largest WAN**.
[13:2:2] - **Uses:** send e-mail, view web pages, connect to servers – **all of the above**.
[13:2:3] - **How it works:** data → **packets**; **IP** directs packets, **TCP** checks errors and reassembles; **DNS** turns names into IP addresses.
[13:2:4] - **"Founder"/pioneer:** **Leonard Kleinrock** (packet-switching theory; first ARPANET message, 1969); Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn designed TCP/IP ("fathers of the Internet").
[13:2:5] # World Wide Web
[13:2:6] - **WWW (W3) = World Wide Web:** collection of **linked information (hypertext documents)** on computers available through the internet; accessed via **HTTP**.
[13:2:7] - **Inventor:** **Tim Berners-Lee** (British), **1989** at **CERN**; he also wrote the **first web browser (named "WorldWideWeb")**, the first web server, HTML, HTTP and URL. Made public in **1991**.
[13:2:8]   - Distractors: Bill Gates, Larry Page, Ted Nelson (coined "hypertext"), Vinod Dham (Pentium), Ray Tomlinson (e-mail), Edward Kasner ("googol").
[13:2:9] - **Hypermedia system:** because it **links to other computer resources** (not because it is "hyper fast").
[13:2:10] - Internet (infrastructure) ≠ WWW (a service running on it).
[13:2:11] # Timeline
[13:2:12] TABLE head: Year | Event
  [13:2:12.0] 1969 | ARPANET – US Department of Defense; forerunner of the internet
  [13:2:12.1] 1984 | OSI model ratified
  [13:2:12.2] 1986 | ERNET – India's academic network
  [13:2:12.3] 1989 | WWW invented by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN
  [13:2:12.4] 1994 | W3C founded
  [13:2:12.5] 1995 | VSNL launched public internet in India on 15 August 1995
  [13:2:12.6] 1998 | Satyam Infoway (Sify) – first private ISP of India; ICANN set up
  [13:2:12.7] 2003 | NIXI set up under MeitY
[13:2:13] # Communication basics
[13:2:14] - **Channel:** the **medium** through which an encoded message is transferred (sender → encoder → **channel** → decoder → receiver).
[13:2:15] - **Networking:** personal computers connected together form a **network**.
[13:2:16] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.30 (Berners-Lee, CERN 1989, first browser and server); PMF S&T Part 5 p.29 (ARPANET 1969, WWW public 1991), p.45 (Internet, TCP/IP, packets, DNS), p.65 (Internet vs WWW); app notes 5:13 sub 0; general knowledge (Kleinrock, VSNL 15 Aug 1995, channel)
## SUB 3 | Protocols, DNS and Domain Names
[13:3:0] - **Protocol:** a **set of rules that governs data communication**; three elements – **syntax** (format), **semantics** (meaning), **timing**.
[13:3:1] # Protocol → function
[13:3:2] TABLE head: Protocol | Function
  [13:3:2.0] TCP/IP | Set of protocols for all transmission exchanges across the internet; the standard protocol suite for internet use/surfing
  [13:3:2.1] HTTP | Hypertext Transfer Protocol – used for accessing the WWW / fetching web pages
  [13:3:2.2] HTTPS | S = Secure – HTTP encrypted with SSL/TLS
  [13:3:2.3] FTP | File Transfer Protocol – exchanging files
  [13:3:2.4] SMTP | Sends e-mail (Application layer)
  [13:3:2.5] POP3 | Downloads mail to one device, usually deletes it from the server
  [13:3:2.6] IMAP | Keeps mail on the server, synced across devices
  [13:3:2.7] DHCP | Assigns IP addresses automatically
  [13:3:2.8] TELNET | Remote login
[13:3:3] - ARPANET is a network, not a protocol; CSMA/CD (Ethernet access method) and FDDI (fibre ring LAN) are not the internet protocol suite.
[13:3:4] # DNS
[13:3:5] - **DNS = Domain Name System** (not "Domain Name Server/Service"): the **database of names and addresses of internet hosts**; converts **domain names → IP addresses**.
[13:3:6] # Domain names
[13:3:7] TABLE head: Extension | Meaning
  [13:3:7.0] .com / .gov / .net | Commercial / government / network – all valid top-level domains
  [13:3:7.1] .edu | Education (.edu.us = educational institute in the USA)
  [13:3:7.2] .au | Australia (Austria = .at, UAE = .ae, Aruba = .aw)
  [13:3:7.3] .in | India (registry run by NIXI)
[13:3:8] - **E-mail address:** username@domainname.extension.
[13:3:9] > ⚠ Trap: HTML is a language, HTTP a protocol; DNS full form = Domain Name **System**.
[13:3:10] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 5 p.45 (TCP/IP, DNS), p.66 (HTTP vs HTTPS, SSL/TLS); app notes 5:13 sub 3; general knowledge (ccTLDs, TELNET, CSMA/CD, FDDI)
## SUB 4 | Network Types and Topologies
[13:4:0] # Network types by area
[13:4:1] TABLE head: Type | Scope / feature
  [13:4:1.0] PAN | Personal area (1-10 m); Bluetooth, smartwatch-phone
  [13:4:1.1] LAN | A single building / small area – home, office, lab; Ethernet is an example (IEEE 802.3)
  [13:4:1.2] CAN | Campus Area Network – several LANs across a campus
  [13:4:1.3] MAN | Metropolitan Area Network – a city
  [13:4:1.4] WAN | Countries/continents; links LANs in different cities; the Internet is the largest WAN
  [13:4:1.5] VPN | Virtual Private Network – secure, encrypted network across the public internet giving users access to their organisation's network
  [13:4:1.6] WLAN | Wireless LAN (Wi-Fi)
[13:4:2] - **VPN (UPSC 2011):** answer (b) – network across the public internet giving access to the organisation's network securely; "shared pool of computing resources" = cloud computing.
[13:4:3] - **Network types vs topologies:** PAN/LAN/CAN/MAN/WAN are **types**; mesh, star, bus, ring are **topologies** (TS Sub Engineers key: **MAN**).
[13:4:4] - **APPSC 2019:** a firm linking LANs in **Mumbai, Bengaluru and New Delhi** uses a **WAN**.
[13:4:5] - **Intranet** = private internal network; **extranet** = controlled extension for partners; **Internet** = network of networks.
[13:4:6] # Topologies
[13:4:7] TABLE head: Topology | Layout | Resilience
  [13:4:7.0] Bus | All nodes on one backbone cable | Backbone break stops the whole network
  [13:4:7.1] Star | All nodes to a central hub/switch | A failed node is only isolated; hub failure stops all
  [13:4:7.2] Ring | Each node linked to two neighbours | One break can disrupt the ring
  [13:4:7.3] Mesh | Every node linked to every other | Most resilient; costliest – n(n-1)/2 links
  [13:4:7.4] Tree | Branching mix of bus and star – a generalisation of the bus topology | Exam key: topology used by the Internet
  [13:4:7.5] Hybrid | Mix of types | The Internet is the largest hybrid topology
[13:4:8] - **Grid** is **not** a common network topology.
[13:4:9] > ⚠ Trap: "Internet topology" – exam keys say **tree**; strictly the Internet is a hybrid (largely mesh) of networks.
[13:4:10] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 5 p.30-35 (PAN, LAN, CAN, MAN, WAN, VPN, topologies), p.33 (UPSC 2011 VPN), p.50 (intranet/extranet); app notes 5:13 sub 1; general knowledge (tree = generalisation of bus, Stallings)
## SUB 5 | IP and MAC Addressing
[13:5:0] TABLE head: Address | Length | Notation
  [13:5:0.0] IPv4 | 32 bits (~4.3 billion addresses) | Dotted decimal, 4 octets each 0-255, e.g. 192.168.1.1
  [13:5:0.1] IPv6 | 128 bits | 8 groups of hexadecimal separated by colons
  [13:5:0.2] MAC (Media Access Control) | 48 bits (6 bytes, 12 hex digits) | Unique ID burnt into the NIC; used at the Data Link layer
[13:5:1] - **IP address** = the unique number that **identifies a computer on the internet** (not e-mail or street address; SMTP/TCP/UDP are protocols).
[13:5:2] - **IPv4 needs fewer bits than IPv6** (32 < 128) (APPSC G1).
[13:5:3] - **Invalid IPv4:** "192.23.350" – only three octets and 350 > 255.
[13:5:4] # IPv4 classes (first octet)
[13:5:5] TABLE head: Class | Range | Use
  [13:5:5.0] A | 1–126 | Large networks
  [13:5:5.1] B | 128–191 | Medium networks
  [13:5:5.2] C | 192–223 | Small networks
  [13:5:5.3] D | 224–239 | Multicast
  [13:5:5.4] E | 240–255 | Experimental
[13:5:6] - **There is no Class F.**
[13:5:7] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 5 p.39 (IP and IP address); app notes 5:13 sub 4; general knowledge (IPv4 octet rule, classes)
## SUB 6 | Internet Connections, Transmission Modes and Wireless Standards
[13:6:0] # Connection types
[13:6:1] TABLE head: Connection | Medium | Speed
  [13:6:1.0] Dial-up | Telephone line + dial-up modem; not always-on | Slowest – up to 56 Kbps
  [13:6:1.1] DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) | Existing telephone lines | 2-24 Mbps
  [13:6:1.2] Cable broadband | Coaxial cable-TV lines (cable modem) | Higher than DSL
  [13:6:1.3] Fibre | Light pulses in optical fibre | 100s of Mbps – Gbps
  [13:6:1.4] Leased line | Dedicated always-on business line | High
  [13:6:1.5] Satellite | GEO (VSAT) / LEO (Starlink, OneWeb); no terrestrial wire | Variable
[13:6:2] - **Wireless web:** internet access from **cellular phones, hand-held and portable gadgets** (Spaceweb, Astroweb, Cosmoweb are not terms).
[13:6:3] # Transmission modes
[13:6:4] TABLE head: Mode | Meaning | Example
  [13:6:4.0] Simplex | One way | Radio/TV broadcast, keyboard
  [13:6:4.1] Half duplex | Both ways, one at a time | Walkie-talkie
  [13:6:4.2] Full duplex | Both ways at once | Telephone call
[13:6:5] - "G" in **2G** = **Generation**; a **podcast** is a radio-style programme shared via the internet.
[13:6:6] # Bluetooth and Wi-Fi
[13:6:7] TABLE head: Feature | Bluetooth | Wi-Fi
  [13:6:7.0] Standard | IEEE 802.15.1 (PAN) | IEEE 802.11 (WLAN)
  [13:6:7.1] Band | 2.4 GHz | 2.4 and 5 GHz (Wi-Fi 6E/7 also 6 GHz)
  [13:6:7.2] Line of sight | Not needed | Not needed
[13:6:8] - **UPSC 2011:** difference = Bluetooth uses 2.4 GHz, Wi-Fi 2.4 or 5 GHz (Bluetooth is PAN, not WLAN; neither needs line of sight).
[13:6:9] - **2.4-2.5 GHz ISM band (UPSC 2010):** **Bluetooth, cordless phones, microwave ovens (2.45 GHz) and Wi-Fi – all four**.
[13:6:10] - **Bluetooth versions:** APPSC key "latest" = **5.1** (2019); then 6.0 (2024, **Channel Sounding**), 6.1 (May 2025), 6.2 (Nov 2025), 6.3 (May 2026), **Core 7.0 (Nov 2026, High Data Throughput)** – the latest as of Nov 2026.
[13:6:11] - **Wi-Fi 7** = **IEEE 802.11be** (2.4, 5 and 6 GHz); **Wi-Fi Direct** links devices with no LAN; **Li-Fi** carries data on **LED light**.
[13:6:12] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 5 p.45 (dial-up 56 Kbps), p.47 (DSL, cable, fibre), p.48 (satellite), p.55-57 (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, UPSC 2011); bluetooth.com blog "Just released: Bluetooth Core 6.3" (6 May 2026); audioxpress.com (Bluetooth HDT in Core 7.0, 4 Nov 2026); app notes 5:13 sub 5-6
## SUB 7 | Internet Governance and India
[13:7:0] TABLE head: Body / Act | Year | Role
  [13:7:0.0] ICANN | 1998 | US non-profit; coordinates the global Domain Name System and IP address allocation
  [13:7:0.1] NIXI (National Internet Exchange of India) | 2003 | Not-for-profit under MeitY; internet exchange points, the .in registry and IRINN
  [13:7:0.2] BhashaNet | 2022 | MeitY and NIXI (not ICANN) – Universal Acceptance for Indian languages; .Bharat in Devanagari
  [13:7:0.3] IT Act, 2000 | 2000 | Sections 69A and 79 – government can order ISPs and intermediaries to block content
  [13:7:0.4] Telecommunications Act, 2023 | 2023 | Replaced the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885; holds the power to suspend internet services
  [13:7:0.5] Orbicom | – | International network of UNESCO Chairs in Communication
[13:7:1] - **Universal Acceptance:** every app and e-mail system accepts all domain names and e-mail IDs, including those in Indian scripts.
[13:7:2] - **7 Apr 2026:** a site opening on one ISP but not another = ISP-level **DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering**.

=== NOTES 5:14 | Ict in Day-to-day Life – Mobile Telephony, Social Media, E-commerce, Digital Media
## SUB 0 | Digital Media, Multimedia and Media Terms
[14:0:0] # Multimedia and digital content
[14:0:1] TABLE head: Item | Fact
  [14:0:1.0] Multimedia | Text, graphics, audio, video, animation, voiceovers combined in one presentation (numeric data alone is not multimedia)
  [14:0:1.1] Podcast | A radio programme shared via the Internet (digital audio to stream or download); internet radio / digital broadcast = live
  [14:0:1.2] e-journals | Published on the Internet
  [14:0:1.3] FCP | Final Cut Pro – Apple's non-linear video editing (production) software; Adobe Premiere Pro also edits video
  [14:0:1.4] Heliodisplay | Air-based (mid-air) display: images projected onto a thin layer of mist/fog, no screen
  [14:0:1.5] Ticker | Strip of scrolling text (headlines, share prices) along the bottom of a television screen
  [14:0:1.6] Referral service | Directing the user to suitable sources of information available elsewhere (library science)
  [14:0:1.7] Specimen | A real object taken out of its natural setting (teaching aid); a model is a replica
[14:0:2] - **Kazaa download:** **Supari** (2003) was the first Bollywood feature sold as a download ($2.99) to Kazaa users (APPSC G1 2004).
[14:0:3] # Media terms (APPSC G2 Mains 2019 set)
[14:0:4] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [14:0:4.0] Infomercial | Paid programming – long TV advertisement looking like a programme
  [14:0:4.1] Innuendo | Defamation by implication; spoken = slander, written = libel
  [14:0:4.2] Semiotics | Study of signs and sign systems (Saussure, Peirce)
  [14:0:4.3] Technological determinism | Technology 'causes' behaviour / drives social change (Marshall McLuhan)
  [14:0:4.4] 'Knowledgeable sources' | Not official, but with access to official information
[14:0:5] # Broadcasting and media organisations
[14:0:6] - **BARC** (Broadcast Audience Research Council, **2015**): measures **TV audiences**, replacing **TAM**; IRS / NRS are readership surveys.
[14:0:7] - **The Wall Street Journal:** business daily from **New York, USA** (Dow Jones, News Corp); **CNN** = **Cable News Network** (US, 1980).
[14:0:8] - **Disney** bought 21st Century Fox's studio and TV assets (deal completed **2019**).
[14:0:9] - **ANI** (1971): first Indian news agency with **syndicated video news**.
[14:0:10] - **DTH** takes signals from **geostationary satellites** straight to home dishes; **DD Free Dish** (Prasar Bharati) – India's **first free DTH**, launched **December 2004** as DD Direct+, renamed 2013.

## SUB 1 | Mobile Telephony – Firsts, Standards and Terms
[14:1:0] # Firsts
[14:1:1] - **First handheld mobile call:** **Martin Cooper** of **Motorola**, **3 April 1973** (to Joel Engel of Bell Labs); so Cooper is credited with inventing the **mobile phone**.
[14:1:2] - **First mobile service in India:** exam key **Hutchison** (Max Touch, Mumbai); India's **first mobile call** was on **Modi Telstra**, Kolkata, **31 July 1995** (Jyoti Basu to Sukh Ram).
[14:1:3] - **Motorola** (March 2003) showed a phone displaying the user's location; **Tata Teleservices PTT** (push-to-talk, May 2004) – then only in USA, Japan, Malaysia (**not Australia**).
[14:1:4] - **QR code:** **Quick Response**, read quickly by a phone camera; designed **1994** (not 1996) by **Denso Wave**, Japan, for the **car industry**.
[14:1:5] - **Mobile Number Portability:** pilot **Haryana**, 25 Nov 2010; pan-India **20 Jan 2011**; full nationwide porting 3 Jul 2015.
[14:1:6] - India = world's **second-largest** telecom market (May 2025).
[14:1:7] # Standards and full forms
[14:1:8] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [14:1:8.0] GSM | Global System for Mobile Communications – 2G digital standard (India 1995)
  [14:1:8.1] CDMA | Code Division Multiple Access
  [14:1:8.2] GPRS | General Packet Radio Service – 2G packet data: Internet on the phone without modem or computer ('GRPS' in the 2003 paper = GPRS)
  [14:1:8.3] LTE | Long-Term Evolution – raises capacity and speed; 4G (uses OFDM and MIMO); WiMAX lost out
  [14:1:8.4] SIM | Subscriber Identity Module
  [14:1:8.5] OTG | On-The-Go (USB OTG: phone acts as USB host)
[14:1:9] - **LTE and IMT-Advanced:** original LTE did **not** meet the ITU **IMT-Advanced** 4G requirements; only **LTE-Advanced** did (UPSC 2010: only statement I correct).
[14:1:10] - Generations: 1G analog → 2G GSM/CDMA → 3G WCDMA → 4G LTE → 5G NR; **6G expected early 2030s**.
[14:1:11] - **Android 16** released for Pixel phones in June 2025; **Pixel Buds** (2017): Google Assistant with real-time translation of **40 languages**.
[14:1:12] # NFC (Near Field Communication)
[14:1:13] - **Contactless** communication using **electromagnetic radio fields** (**not light waves**); range **a few centimetres** (~4 cm, not a metre); can **encrypt**; built into **smartphones**.
[14:1:14] - Speed **106–424 kbps**; easier pairing and **lower power than Bluetooth**; RBI allows **offline UPI Lite** payments over NFC; RuPay tap-and-pay.
[14:1:15] > UPSC 2015: "a metre apart" ✗ → answer **a and c only**; APPSC: "uses light waves" = the untrue statement.
[14:1:16] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 5 p.35-36, p.40, p.98-99; app notes 5:14 sub 0; web search (Modi Telstra 1995); general knowledge (Motorola 2003, PTT, OTG, Pixel Buds)
## SUB 2 | E-mail and Video Conferencing
[14:2:0] # E-mail
[14:2:1] - **E-mail** = **Electronic Mail**; address = **user name @ domain name** – in mark.sttol@ITdesk.info the **domain is ITdesk.info**.
[14:2:2] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [14:2:2.0] SMTP | Sends mail
  [14:2:2.1] POP3 / IMAP | Receive mail
  [14:2:2.2] CC | Sends copies (all see each other)
  [14:2:2.3] BCC | Blind carbon copy – hides recipients' addresses from one another
  [14:2:2.4] Video mail | Pre-recorded video by e-mail – can carry graphics, video clips, video messages (all)
  [14:2:2.5] Finger | Protocol/command to find a user's e-mail address and login details (Archie = FTP file search)
  [14:2:2.6] Listserv | Mailing list linking people with similar interests worldwide
  [14:2:2.7] Instant messaging | Real-time messages between two or more people
[14:2:3] - **Free e-mail providers:** **Hotmail, Rediffmail, Yahoo** (and Gmail) – all free.
[14:2:4] - **Rajasthan:** first state to give residents a **free e-mail address in Hindi** (2016).
[14:2:5] # Video conferencing
[14:2:6] - **Live two-way video and audio** between two or more places using telecom technology (with data).
[14:2:7] - **Essentials:** **video camera, display, microphone**, speaker, broadband, codec software; a **telephone is not essential** (nor an RFID reader).
[14:2:8] > Match (FSO): e-mail = instant delivery with attachments; listserv = similar interests; video conferencing = video + audio + data; instant messaging = real-time exchange.
[14:2:9] ~~ Sources: app notes 5:14 sub 3; general knowledge (Finger, listserv, free e-mail, Rajasthan Hindi e-mail)

## SUB 5 | E-commerce
[14:5:0] TABLE head: Model | Who trades | Example
  [14:5:0.0] B2B | Business to business | IndiaMART, M. Junction
  [14:5:0.1] B2C | Business to consumer | Flipkart, Amazon, Alibaba

  [14:5:0.3] D2C | Brand sells directly, no middleman | –

[14:5:2] - **FDI:** **100% automatic route in the marketplace model**; **none in the inventory model**.
[14:5:3] - **ONDC** (Open Network for Digital Commerce): an **open, network-based protocol**, not a platform or payment gateway; links any buyer app to any seller app (B2C and B2B); **beta-tested in Bengaluru**.

## SUB 6 | Laws on Digital Platforms
[14:6:0] TABLE head: Act / rules | Year | Provision
  [14:6:0.0] Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules | 2020 | Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019; grievance officer; display country of origin
  [14:6:0.1] IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules | 2021 | Under Section 87 of the IT Act; replaced 2011 rules; social media, OTT, digital news; three-tier grievance redressal
  [14:6:0.2] IT Amendment Rules | 2023 | Ignoring orders on false content → loss of safe harbour (Section 79)
  [14:6:0.3] Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act | 2025 | Bans real-money gaming; Online Gaming Authority of India – attached office of MeitY; rules effective 1 May 2026
  [14:6:0.4] Code on Social Security | 2020 | Gig and platform workers defined first; in force with all four labour codes from 21 Nov 2025
  [14:6:0.5] DPDP Act | 2023 | Child = below 18; verifiable parental consent (Section 9)
[14:6:1] - Proposed law on social-media access: **graded, age-based limits**, not a blanket ban.

=== NOTES 5:15 | Ict and Industry – Industry 4.0, Internet of Things, Robotics and Automation
## SUB 0 | Robotics and Automation
[15:0:0] # Basics
[15:0:1] - **Robotics:** interdisciplinary – mechanical, electrical/electronics, computer engineering; **Mechatronics** = mechanical engineering + electronics + robotics/computing (product engineering).
[15:0:2] - **CAM (Computer-Aided Manufacturing):** computers assist in **all operations of a manufacturing plant** (planning, control); paired with CAD.
[15:0:3] TABLE head: Type | Use
  [15:0:3.0] Industrial | Welding, painting, assembly, packaging
  [15:0:3.1] Service | Hospitality, retail, reception; domestic (vacuum cleaners)
  [15:0:3.2] Surgical / medical | Robotic surgery, rehabilitation
  [15:0:3.3] Humanoid | Human-like form (Manav, Vyommitra, Optimus)
  [15:0:3.4] Cobots | Work safely beside humans (Industry 4.0)
[15:0:4] - **Advantages:** help people with **disabilities**, work in **dangerous environments**, **never tire**. **Disadvantage:** **job displacement** ("can replace jobs" is NOT an advantage).
[15:0:5] - **ISO 10218** = safety norms for **industrial robots**.
[15:0:6] # Robots → developer and purpose
[15:0:7] TABLE head: Robot | Developer | Purpose
  [15:0:7.0] BRABO | TAL Manufacturing (Tata), 2017 | First 'Made in India' industrial robot
  [15:0:7.1] Manav | Diwakar Vaish, A-SET Training & Research Institutes, Delhi (2014) | India's first 3D-printed humanoid
  [15:0:7.2] SSI Mantra | SS Innovations (Dr Sudhir Srivastava) | First Made-in-India surgical robotic system; first installed at Rajiv Gandhi Cancer Institute and Research Centre, Delhi (2022)
  [15:0:7.3] HomoSEP | IIT Madras (2022) | Cleans septic tanks without humans
  [15:0:7.4] Bandicoot | Genrobotics, Kerala | Cleans manholes and sewers (manual scavenging)
  [15:0:7.5] Beta Tank robots | Beta Tank Robotics, Bengaluru (IIT Guwahati-incubated), Feb 2023 | Clean petrochemical tanks; key: hydraulically powered and controlled
  [15:0:7.6] Vyommitra | ISRO | Half-humanoid for the uncrewed Gaganyaan flight
  [15:0:7.7] Daksh | DRDO | Remotely operated robot to defuse IEDs
  [15:0:7.8] HRP-Chromet | Japan (2008) | Small humanoid robot
  [15:0:7.9] Optimus | Tesla (prototype humanoid; new version 2023) | General-purpose humanoid
[15:0:8] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 7 book p.711-714; app notes 5:15 sub 5; web search (Beta Tank, Feb 2023); general knowledge (BRABO, HRP-Chromet, Optimus, CAM, RGCI)
## SUB 1 | Semiconductors and Indigenous Chips
[15:1:0] # Basics
[15:1:1] - **Silicon** = the **semiconductor** used for computer (IC) chips (exam key for "newest substance in chips"; strictly **gallium arsenide** is the newer compound semiconductor).
[15:1:2] - **Not a semiconductor:** **Krypton** (noble gas); silicon, germanium, selenium are.
[15:1:3] - **p-type:** trivalent doping → **holes** = majority carriers; n-type → electrons.
[15:1:4] - **Diode:** current one way only → **AC to DC** (rectification); a **semiconductor diode is non-ohmic** (copper coil, heater coil, rheostat are ohmic).
[15:1:5] - **Silicon carbide** (carborundum): very hard → abrasive for **cutting very hard substances**; also a power semiconductor.
[15:1:6] - **Piezoelectric MEMS** (May 2023): **IIT Madras + DRDO** (NPOL) – PZT thin-film **underwater** acoustic sensor for Navy SONAR.
[15:1:7] # Indigenous processors → developer
[15:1:8] TABLE head: Processor | Developer | Feature
  [15:1:8.0] IRIS | IIT Madras + ISRO (Feb 2025) | Indigenous RISC-V Controller for Space – SHAKTI-based aerospace chip
  [15:1:8.1] SHAKTI | IIT Madras | RISC-V
  [15:1:8.2] DHRUV64 | C-DAC | 64-bit RISC-V
  [15:1:8.3] AJIT | IIT Bombay | Indigenous processor
  [15:1:8.4] Vikram 3201 | ISRO's Semi-Conductor Laboratory, Chandigarh | 32-bit space-grade (2025)
[15:1:9] # India Semiconductor Mission
[15:1:10] - **ISM** launched **2021**, **₹76,000 crore** PLI outlay.
[15:1:11] TABLE head: Unit | Type | State
  [15:1:11.0] Micron, Sanand | ATMP | Gujarat
  [15:1:11.1] Tata-PSMC, Dholera | Wafer fab (the only true fab) | Gujarat
  [15:1:11.2] Tata, Jagiroad (Morigaon) | ATMP | Assam
  [15:1:11.3] Kaynes Semicon, Sanand | OSAT | Gujarat
[15:1:12] - **Semicon 2.0** (ISM Phase 2, 2 Sep 2026): **₹1,27,500 crore**; CMOS fabs up to **40%** capital subsidy; R&D up to 75%.
[15:1:13] - **AP pitch** (Jun 2026): **Sri Sathya Sai district** for aerospace, drone and semiconductor manufacturing.
[15:1:14] ~~ Sources: app notes 5:15 sub 6; www.iitm.ac.in press release 10 May 2023 (piezo MEMS); general knowledge (semiconductor physics, SiC, IRIS)
## SUB 2 | Extended Reality, Metaverse and Haptics
[15:2:0] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [15:2:0.0] Virtual Reality (VR) | Fully computer-generated, immersive world that shuts out the real one; the user is still a real person
  [15:2:0.1] Augmented Reality (AR) | Digital content overlaid on the real world via a phone/PC camera (Pokemon Go); does not block the physical world
  [15:2:0.2] Mixed Reality (MR) | Real and virtual objects interact in real time
  [15:2:0.3] Extended Reality (XR) | Umbrella for VR + AR + MR
  [15:2:0.4] Metaverse | Interoperable network of 3D virtual worlds, accessed by millions at once, with property rights over virtual items (UPSC 2024)
  [15:2:0.5] Haptic technology | Tactile feedback – recreates touch by forces, vibrations or motions
[15:2:1] - **UPSC 2019:** "AR shuts out the physical world" ✗ (that is VR); "VR projects images onto real objects" ✗ (that is AR) → **3 and 4 only**.
[15:2:2] - Thomas Caudell (Boeing) coined "augmented reality" (1990); **VARCoE** at IIT Bhubaneswar; **IMAGE CoE** at Hyderabad.
[15:2:3] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 7 book p.785-787; app notes 5:15 sub 4; general knowledge (haptics)
## SUB 3 | 3D Printing
[15:3:0] - **Additive manufacturing:** objects built **layer by layer** from a **CAD** model; opposite of subtractive machining; **4D printing** adds materials that **change shape over time**.
[15:3:1] - **Applications (UPSC 2018 key: all five):** **confectionery**, **bionic ears**, **automotive industry**, **reconstructive surgery**, data-processing technologies; also aerospace, construction, implants.
[15:3:2] - **Surgery:** 3D printing gives the surgeon a **physical model of the patient's anatomy** (surgical planning).
[15:3:3] - **India's first 3D-printed post office:** **Bengaluru** (Cambridge Layout, near Ulsoor), **2023**; 1,021 sq ft, built in **43 days**.
[15:3:4] > ⚠ Disputed: PMF IAS (book p.772) prints (a) 1, 3 and 4 only for the 2018 question; the UPSC key and most books give (d) all five.
[15:3:5] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 7 book p.770-772; app notes 5:15 sub 8
## SUB 4 | Internet of Things, RFID and Wearables
[15:4:0] # IoT
[15:4:1] - **IoT:** sensor-equipped devices sharing data over a network **without human intervention**; term by **Kevin Ashton** (1999).
[15:4:2] - **Agriculture (APPSC FRO 2022 A-R):** traditional farming is labour-intensive (A true); IoT sensors offer an alternative (R true) – **R does not explain A**.
[15:4:3] TABLE head: Layer | Job
  [15:4:3.0] Perception | Senses (sensors, RFID)
  [15:4:3.1] Network | Transmits
  [15:4:3.2] Application | Smart services
[15:4:4] - Four-stage version adds a **transport** layer.
[15:4:5] TABLE head: Variant | Concerns
  [15:4:5.0] IIoT | Industrial automation
  [15:4:5.1] IoNT | Nano-devices
  [15:4:5.2] Internet of Mobile Things | Mobile objects (not assembly lines)
  [15:4:5.3] Mission-critical IoT | Military applications
[15:4:6] - **IoT vs AI:** smart thermostat, fitness wearable = **IoT**; chatbot, image recognition = **AI** (analyses and decides).
[15:4:7] - Uses: **smart farming, homes, grids**, cities, healthcare; **NDCP 2018** covers 5G, IoT, M2M; IoT CoEs (MeitY-NASSCOM): Bengaluru, Gurugram, Gandhinagar, Visakhapatnam.
[15:4:8] # RFID
[15:4:9] TABLE head: Tag | Power | Reply
  [15:4:9.0] Passive | No battery – powered by the reader's field | Backscatters the reader's signal
  [15:4:9.1] Semi-passive | Battery runs the chip only | Uses the reader's radio waves to reply
  [15:4:9.2] Active | Own battery and transmitter | Broadcasts itself, long range
[15:4:10] - RFID needs **no line of sight** within range → APPSC G1: **II and IV only** correct.
[15:4:11] # Wearables
[15:4:12] - Smartwatches, fitness bands: **location**, **sleep monitoring**, heart rate; **hearing aids** for the hearing impaired → UPSC 2019: **I, II and III**.
[15:4:13] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 5 p.66-67; PMF S&T Part 7 book p.773-774; app notes 5:15 sub 2-3
## SUB 5 | Drones, UAVs and eVTOL
[15:5:0] - **UAV types:** multirotor (quadcopter), **fixed-wing**, single-rotor, hybrid **VTOL**; **not all** land vertically, hover automatically or run on battery only → UPSC 2025: **none** correct.
[15:5:1] - **eVTOL** = electric Vertical Take-Off and Landing aircraft (air taxis) → **aviation**.
[15:5:2] TABLE head: Drone Rules, 2021 class | Weight
  [15:5:2.0] Nano | up to 250 g
  [15:5:2.1] Micro | 250 g – 2 kg
  [15:5:2.2] Small | 2–25 kg
  [15:5:2.3] Medium | 25–150 kg
  [15:5:2.4] Large | above 150 kg
[15:5:3] - **Swarms:** many drones coordinated by software (surveillance, light shows, strikes).
[15:5:4] - **Drone hub by 2030:** Drone Rules 2021, **DigitalSky**, **PLI ₹120 crore** (2021), **Drone Shakti**, DGCA-approved training institutes.
[15:5:5] - **Kisan drones:** spraying and land mapping; **100** flagged off Feb 2022. **Namo Drone Didi:** drones to **women SHGs**; ₹1,261 crore (2023-24 to 2025-26) for **15,000** SHGs.
[15:5:6] - **AP Drone City:** **Orvakal, Kurnool**.
[15:5:7] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 6 p.86-88; app notes 5:15 sub 7
## SUB 6 | Industry 4.0 and Automation Terms
[15:6:0] TABLE head: Stage | Defining technology
  [15:6:0.0] Industry 1.0 | Mechanisation, steam (steam looms)
  [15:6:0.1] Industry 2.0 | Electricity, mass production, assembly line
  [15:6:0.2] Industry 3.0 | Automation, computers and electronics
  [15:6:0.3] Industry 4.0 | Cyber-physical systems, IoT, AI, big data; smart factories
  [15:6:0.4] Industry 5.0 | Human-machine collaboration
[15:6:1] - **'Industry 4.0'** coined in **Germany** (Hannover Fair, 2011); **'Fourth Industrial Revolution'** – **Klaus Schwab** (WEF), 2016.
[15:6:2] - **SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0** – **Ministry of Heavy Industries**; **NM-ICPS** – **25 Technology Innovation Hubs**.
[15:6:3] - **AP:** WEF 4IR Centre would be India's **third** (after Mumbai and Telangana).
[15:6:4] - **Criticism:** automation and AI replace **intellectual as well as manual** work.
[15:6:5] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [15:6:5.0] PLC | Programmable Logic Controller
  [15:6:5.1] SCADA | Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition – remote monitoring of plants and grids
  [15:6:5.2] Digital twin | Virtual replica for simulation and monitoring
  [15:6:5.3] Cyber-physical system | Computing joined with physical processes
  [15:6:5.4] Cobot | Collaborative robot
  [15:6:5.5] mMTC | 5G slice for dense IoT sensors
[15:6:6] ~~ Sources: app notes 5:15 sub 0-1

## SUB 1 | Quantum Computing and Supercomputers
[17:1:0] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [17:1:0.0] Qubit | Basic unit of quantum information – context of quantum computing (UPSC 2022)
  [17:1:0.1] Superposition | A quantum system can be in multiple states at once until measured (qubit = 0 and 1)
  [17:1:0.2] Entanglement | Links qubits' states regardless of distance
  [17:1:0.3] Decoherence | Loss of quantum state to the environment – main barrier
  [17:1:0.4] Shor's algorithm / Q-Day | Can break public-key cryptography; Q-Day = when it becomes able to
[17:1:1] - **Applications:** **cryptography**, **drug discovery**, **financial modelling**, logistics, materials – **not desktop publishing**.
[17:1:2] TABLE head: Machine | Fact
  [17:1:2.0] Micius (QUESS), China, 16 Aug 2016 | World's first quantum communication satellite
  [17:1:2.1] Google Sycamore (2019) | Quantum supremacy – a set task in ~200 s
  [17:1:2.2] Jiuzhang (China, 2020) | Photonic supremacy machine
  [17:1:2.3] Fugaku (Japan) | World's fastest supercomputer 2020-21 (exam key for "least time to calculate")
  [17:1:2.4] Pratyush (IITM Pune, 2018) | India's fastest supercomputer as of March 2018
[17:1:3] - **National Quantum Mission:** approved **19 Apr 2023**; **₹6,003.65 crore** (2023-24 to 2030-31); **50–1,000 physical qubits** in 8 years; **four thematic hubs** – computing, communication, sensing & metrology, materials & devices (not quantum biology).
[17:1:4] - **2025** = UN **International Year of Quantum Science and Technology** (centenary of quantum mechanics); **World Quantum Day = 14 April**.
[17:1:5] - 2026 items: Raman Research Institute – a timed local "quantum flip" delays **entanglement sudden death**; **Microsoft Majorana 2** – qubit stability 20–60 s.
[17:1:6] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 7 p.59-69; app notes 5:17 sub 5; general knowledge, not checked (Micius, Pratyush, Sycamore)
## SUB 2 | Turing Test and AI Milestones
[17:2:0] - **Turing test:** Alan Turing (1950, *Computing Machinery and Intelligence*) – checks whether a machine's replies can be told apart from a human's; original name **"the Imitation Game"** (not LISP or the Halting Problem).
[17:2:1] - **Term "AI":** **John McCarthy**, Dartmouth **1956**. **Colossus** (1943–45): Tommy Flowers.
[17:2:2] - **Robotics** = technology most closely associated with "artificial intelligence" (exam key).
[17:2:3] TABLE head: Emerging technology | Person
  [17:2:3.0] Artificial intelligence | Alan Turing
  [17:2:3.1] OpenAI | Sam Altman
  [17:2:3.2] Internet of Things | Kevin Ashton
  [17:2:3.3] Augmented reality | Thomas P. Caudell
[17:2:4] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.29-30; app notes 5:17 sub 0
## SUB 3 | Advanced Materials and Nanotechnology
[17:3:0] - **Bulletproof material:** **Kevlar** – an **aramid** (para-aromatic **polyamide**) fibre; lightweight bulletproof **helmets and jackets** (not nylon, rayon, Dacron, Terylene, Bakelite, Teflon).
[17:3:1] - **Bhabha Kavach** (International Police Expo, July 2019): **India's lightest bulletproof jacket** (BARC technology).
[17:3:2] - **Titanium** = "**metal of the future**" – light, strong, corrosion-resistant (aerospace, implants).
[17:3:3] TABLE head: Material / innovation | Fact / developer

=== NOTES 5:19 | Blockchain, Distributed Ledger, Cryptocurrency and Cbdc (e-rupee)
## SUB 0 | Cryptocurrency and Bitcoin
[19:0:0] - **Cryptocurrency:** money transfers secured with **encryption (cryptography)**, peer-to-peer, **without a central bank** (not legal tender, RTGS, NEFT).
[19:0:1] - **Bitcoin** (**2009**): first cryptocurrency, by pseudonymous **Satoshi Nakamoto**; decentralised; coins created by **mining** (complex software / computation).
[19:0:2] - **UPSC 2016:** Bitcoins are **not tracked by central banks** ✗; anyone with an address can send/receive ✓; payments possible **without either side knowing the other's identity** ✓ → **2 and 3 only**.
[19:0:3] - **CDS 2017:** decentralised ✓, generated by complex software ✓, **RBI never recognised it as legal tender** ✗ → **I and II**.
[19:0:4] - **Japan:** recognised Bitcoin as a **legal payment method from 1 April 2017**.
[19:0:5] - **BuyUcoin:** first Indian platform for **wholesale crypto trading** (April 2019).
[19:0:6] - **Not a cryptocurrency:** the **Yen** (Japan's fiat currency).
[19:0:7] - India: crypto **not legal tender**; VDA providers under **PMLA (March 2023)**; **30%** tax on VDA gains (**Sec 115BBH**, Finance Act **2022**) + **1% TDS** (**Sec 194S**); losses cannot be set off.
[19:0:8] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 7 p.113-116; NextGen S&T G2 Part 1 p.26; gktoday.in 25 Apr 2019 (BuyUcoin); app notes 5:19 sub 2; general knowledge, not checked (Japan 2017)
## SUB 1 | Blockchain and Distributed Ledger
[19:1:0] - **Blockchain:** a **time-stamped series of immutable records** managed by a **cluster of computers not owned by any single entity**; first introduced in **Bitcoin** (Satoshi Nakamoto).
[19:1:1] - **UPSC 2020:** public ledger everyone can inspect, no single user controls ✓; data only about cryptocurrency ✗; apps can be built **without anybody's permission** ✓ → **1 and 3 only**.
[19:1:2] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [19:1:2.0] Distributed ledger | Shared ledger copied across nodes; single source of truth; no central validator
  [19:1:2.1] Block | Transactions + timestamp + hash of the previous block (not private keys)
  [19:1:2.2] Hash / node | Cryptographic fingerprint of a block / a computer holding a ledger copy
  [19:1:2.3] Immutability | Cannot be altered without consensus – no central authority changes data
  [19:1:2.4] Consensus | Rule by which nodes agree on valid transactions
[19:1:3] - Stakeholders **hold copies** and changes need **consensus** – so records are visible but not alterable.
[19:1:4] - **Uses:** land records, certificates, supply chain, **e-voting**, health records, e-Notary, farm insurance.
[19:1:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T G2 Part 1 p.26; PMF S&T Part 7 p.107, p.111-112; app notes 5:19 sub 0

=== NOTES 5:20 | Telecom Technologies – 3G to 5G, 6G Roadmap, Satellite Communication, Optical Fibre
## SUB 0 | Electromagnetic Spectrum – Order, Uses and Wave Basics
[20:0:0] # Order of the spectrum
[20:0:1] TABLE head: Wave | Wavelength | Frequency | Main uses
  [20:0:1.0] Radio | > 1 m (longest) | < 3 × 10⁸ Hz (lowest) | AM/FM radio, TV, mobile, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, MRI; satellite links (radio family)
  [20:0:1.1] Microwave | 1 mm – 1 m | 300 MHz – 300 GHz | Satellite communication, radar, 5G, point-to-point telecom links, ovens
  [20:0:1.2] Infrared | 700 nm – 1 mm |  | TV/AC remotes, night vision, physiotherapy (muscle pain, paralysis), heaters
  [20:0:1.3] Visible | ~400–700 nm (violet shortest, red longest) |  | Vision, Li-Fi/VLC, optical fibre (some)
  [20:0:1.4] Ultraviolet | 10–400 nm |  | Sterilisation (UV lamps, semen straws, water), forgery detection on currency, vitamin D; sunscreens block UV
  [20:0:1.5] X-rays | 0.01–10 nm |  | Radiography, CT, baggage scans, cracks in metals
  [20:0:1.6] Gamma | < 0.01 nm (shortest) | highest | Radiotherapy, sterilising instruments
[20:0:2] - **Energy and frequency rise** Radio < Microwave < IR < Visible < UV < **X-ray** < **Gamma**; photon energy E = hν, so shorter wavelength = more energy (200–280 nm UV beats 280–400 nm; **blue** beats green, yellow, red).
[20:0:3] - **Decreasing frequency:** **Gamma > X-rays > UV > Radio**. Longest wavelength: **radio**; smallest among X-ray/visible/IR/microwave: **X-rays**; among radio/visible/IR/UV: **UV**.
[20:0:4] - Visible light range: **400–700 nm** (also given as **390–780 nm**; VLC uses 375–780 nm).
[20:0:5] - **Visible > X-ray in wavelength; X-ray photons > UV photons > visible photons in energy.**
[20:0:6] - **X-rays** are uncharged EM waves: **not deflected** by electric or magnetic fields; high penetration; wavelength far below visible.
[20:0:7] - **Red** is used in danger/traffic signals: **longest wavelength**, least scattered, seen from far.
[20:0:8] - **TV remote:** common remotes use **infrared** (some use radio). **Telecommunication** links: **microwaves**; **radar**: **microwaves**.
[20:0:9] # Wave basics and sound
[20:0:10] - **Wavelength** = distance between **two successive crests or troughs**.
[20:0:11] - EM waves are transverse and need no medium; **sound** is mechanical and **longitudinal** (radio, X-ray, gamma are EM).
[20:0:12] - **Supersonic waves are not electromagnetic.** **Sonic boom** = shock-wave bang from an object faster than sound (**supersonic aircraft**).
[20:0:13] - Sound travels **faster in steel (~5,000–6,000 m/s) than in air (~343 m/s)** – a listener at the rail hears a blow twice.
[20:0:14] > Exam angle: "which has the highest energy / longest wavelength / decreasing frequency" – about 25 PYQs (UPSC, UPPSC, RAS, NDA, CDS, SSC).
[20:0:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Sheets Physics p.57-62, p.76, p.81; PMF S&T Part 5 p.54-58; app notes 5:20 sub 7
## SUB 1 | Optical Fibre and Total Internal Reflection
[20:1:0] # Total internal reflection (TIR)
[20:1:1] - Conditions: light goes from **denser → rarer** medium **and** angle of incidence **> critical angle**; light is reflected **with no loss of intensity**.
[20:1:2] - Refractive index: **Diamond (~2.42) > sapphire (~1.77) > dense flint glass > glass (~1.5) > fused quartz > water > air** – so TIR is possible **diamond → glass**, **diamond → air**, never air → water/glass.
[20:1:3] - Higher refractive index = **slower light** (among glass, water, air, vacuum: slowest in **glass**).
[20:1:4] TABLE head: Phenomenon / device | Principle
  [20:1:4.0] Optical fibre | TIR (successive TIRs let light follow a bent, zig-zag path)
  [20:1:4.1] Endoscope | Bundle of optical fibres, TIR
  [20:1:4.2] Brilliance of diamond | TIR (critical angle ≈ 24.4°)
  [20:1:4.3] Mirage (desert) | TIR in hot, rarer air near the ground
  [20:1:4.4] Glass beads on traffic signs | TIR (A and R both true, R explains)
  [20:1:4.5] Crack in glass seen obliquely | Looks silvery (TIR)
  [20:1:4.6] Rainbow | Dispersion + (total) internal reflection + refraction
  [20:1:4.7] Stick bent in water | Refraction (not scattering)
  [20:1:4.8] Sea looks blue | Reflection of sky + scattering of light by water
[20:1:5] # Optical fibre communication
[20:1:6] - Thin strand of **glass (silica)** or plastic; **core (higher n) + cladding (lower n)**; signal travels as **pulses of light (light waves)**.
[20:1:7] - **Fastest** medium vs copper, radio, satellite; main use **communication** (telecom, internet); very **low power**, **free from radio-frequency interference**.
[20:1:8] - In India **Sterlite (Sterlite Tech)** makes optical fibre (not Reliance). **Single-mode** = long distances; **multi-mode** = short runs.
[20:1:9] # Undersea cables and national fibre
[20:1:10] - Undersea cables ~**1.5 million km**, carry ~**99%** of international traffic.
[20:1:11] - **CANI** (Chennai–Andaman and Nicobar Islands), ~2,300 km, BSNL, inaugurated **10 Aug 2020**.
[20:1:12] - **NOFN** (approved 25 Oct 2011) → **BharatNet**: all **2,50,000 Gram Panchayats**, funded by **USOF** (now Digital Bharat Nidhi), **not NIIF**.
[20:1:13] - PM Gati Shakti NMP (2026): ~**13.5 lakh** route km OFC; **PM-WANI 3.15 lakh** hotspots.
[20:1:14] > Exam angle: "optical fibre works on…" = TIR – asked about 15 times.
[20:1:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Sheets Physics p.25, p.27, p.65-69, p.73; NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 3 p.7-8; PMF S&T Part 5 p.47; app notes 5:20 sub 6
## SUB 2 | Mobile Generations, GSM Family and LTE
[20:2:0] # Generations
[20:2:1] TABLE head: Generation | Core technology / feature
  [20:2:1.0] 1G | Analog, FDMA
  [20:2:1.1] 2G | Digital; GSM (TDMA) and CDMA; SMS (G = Generation)
  [20:2:1.2] 2.5G / 2.75G | GPRS / EDGE (GSM data)
  [20:2:1.3] 3G | CDMA-based (WCDMA/CDMA2000)
  [20:2:1.4] 4G | LTE = Long Term Evolution, OFDMA; VoLTE = voice carried over the LTE data network
  [20:2:1.5] 5G | NR = New Radio; latency as low as 1 ms
  [20:2:1.6] 6G | Early 2030s; "omnipresent wireless intelligence"
[20:2:2] - India's cellular technologies: **GSM and CDMA**.
[20:2:3] - **GSM family:** GPRS, EDGE, LTE (UPSC 2010: II, III, IV); **DSL is wired** (telephone line), not GSM.
[20:2:4] - UPSC 2019: LTE is **4G** (not "3G"), and VoLTE is not "voice-only" → **neither** statement correct.
[20:2:5] - **WLL** = Wireless Local Loop; TRAI prefers **C-V2X** for vehicle communication.
[20:2:6] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 5 p.37-44, p.47; app notes 5:20 sub 1
## SUB 3 | 5G in India and the 6G Roadmap
[20:3:0] # 5G
[20:3:1] - **World's first 5G:** **South Korea, April 2019** (commercial launch 3–5 April 2019).
[20:3:2] - **India:** launched by the PM on **1 Oct 2022** at **India Mobile Congress**; **Hyderabad** among the first cities (with Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Bengaluru, Varanasi…).
[20:3:3] - **Indigenous 5G Test Bed** (DoT grant, 2018): multi-institute project led by IIT Madras at five locations (IIT Madras, IIT Delhi, IIT Hyderabad, IIT Kanpur, IISc) – true, but it does not explain the launch date.
[20:3:4] - **Jio** 5G partners: Meta, Google, Microsoft, Intel, Qualcomm; Jio + Google: affordable 5G smartphones.
[20:3:5] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [20:3:5.0] sub-6 GHz | Wider coverage, better penetration
  [20:3:5.1] mmWave | Very high data rates, short range
  [20:3:5.2] Network slicing | One physical network split into several virtual networks
  [20:3:5.3] 5G Standalone (SA) | No 4G core → lower latency
  [20:3:5.4] VoNR | Voice over New Radio: voice on the 5G network itself (replaces 2G/3G/VoLTE voice)
[20:3:6] - 5G enables **IoT, edge computing, network slicing**, AR/VR, remote surgery.
[20:3:7] - **5G & Beyond Hackathon 2023:** announced by **DoT (not DST)** in June 2023; open to individuals, students, start-ups, academia; **100 winners share Rs 1 crore** (Rs 1 lakh each).
[20:3:8] - Open-RAN 5G: **Airtel–Tata**; **TTDF** (2022) gets **5% of Digital Bharat Nidhi**; **C-DOT** set up **1984**.
[20:3:9] - **AP:** **IIITDM Kurnool** ranked **1st among 100 5G Use Case Labs** (DoT gradation Jan–Jun 2026, all four categories).
[20:3:10] # 6G
[20:3:11] - **Bharat 6G Vision** (PM, **March 2023**): India to lead 6G design, development and deployment by **2030**; **Bharat 6G Alliance** launched **2023**.
[20:3:12] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 5 p.29, p.44; dqindia.com 'DoT launches 5G and Beyond Hackathon 2023' (10 Jul 2023; Rs 1 lakh per winner); DoT press release (100 winners, Rs 1 crore pool – seen in search result only); app notes 5:20 sub 0-3
## SUB 4 | Wireless Access – Li-Fi, Wi-Fi, WiMAX, Bluetooth
[20:4:0] TABLE head: Li-Fi (Light Fidelity) | Wi-Fi
  [20:4:0.0] Visible light from LEDs; term by Harald Haas (2011) | Radio waves (2.4 / 5 GHz)
  [20:4:0.1] Faster, more bandwidth, secure, no EM interference | Longer range
  [20:4:0.2] Does not pass through walls | Passes through walls
[20:4:1] - **VLC** (UPSC 2020): 375–780 nm, **faster than Bluetooth**, **no EM interference**, but **short-range** (not long-range) → **1, 3, 4**.
[20:4:2] - **WiMAX** = World Wide Interoperability for **Microwave Access** (IEEE 802.16), **communication technology**, mainly **2–3.5 GHz**.
[20:4:3] - **Bluetooth:** short-range **radio waves**, 2.4 GHz ISM band; secure **Personal Area Networks**; developed **1994** by **Jaap Haartsen**; wireless link between equipment.
[20:4:4] - **2.4 GHz ISM band** (licence-free): Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, cordless phones, microwave ovens – **not FM radio**.
[20:4:5] - **Wi-Fi 6 = 802.11ax; Wi-Fi 7 = 802.11be.**
[20:4:6] - **Short-range devices** (UPSC 2022): **CCTV, RFID and WLAN** – all three. **CCTV** = Closed-Circuit Television. **RFID**: radio tags (Kavach track tags). **FSO**: data by laser beams through the air.
[20:4:7] - **Project Loon** (Google/Alphabet): stratospheric helium **balloons** for internet = **wireless communication**; shut Jan 2021.
[20:4:8] - **Mumbai Central:** first station with Google free public Wi-Fi (**Jan 2016**). India **49th** in Network Readiness Index 2024 (from 60th).
[20:4:9] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 5 p.35, p.47, p.55-57, p.60-62; app notes 5:20 sub 8
## SUB 5 | Satellite Communication and Radio Propagation
[20:5:0] - Satellite communication works through **transponders** (receive uplink, amplify, retransmit downlink) and uses **microwaves** (radio family; SSC keys say "radio waves").
[20:5:1] TABLE head: Mode | Bands | Use
  [20:5:1.0] Ground wave | LF/MF | AM radio
  [20:5:1.1] Sky wave (ionosphere reflects) | HF 3–30 MHz | Shortwave radio – very distant stations
  [20:5:1.2] Space wave (line of sight) | VHF, UHF 300 MHz–3 GHz, microwaves | UHF = cellular phones (also TV, GPS); satellites
[20:5:2] - Dish TV fails in rain: raindrops **absorb** and **scatter** the energy; a **small antenna** cannot pick up the weakened signal.
[20:5:3] TABLE head:  | GEO | LEO
  [20:5:3.0] Altitude | ~35,786 km | Below ~2,000 km
  [20:5:3.1] Latency | Higher | Low
  [20:5:3.2] Examples | GSAT | Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb (Bharti), Amazon Kuiper
[20:5:4] - **Starlink** (8,000+ satellites): **GMPCS** (Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite) licence **2025**; user terminals **made in India within 5 years**.
[20:5:5] - **Telecommunications Act 2023:** licensing → **authorisation**; terrestrial spectrum **auctioned**, satellite spectrum **assigned administratively**. ITU: de-orbit within **25 years**.
[20:5:6] - **SREESAT-1** (SNIST Hyderabad students, 2019): **balloon-based** environment monitor (temperature, pressure, humidity, UV/IR) – not a drone or Wi-Fi system.
[20:5:7] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 5 p.55-59; NextGen Rocket Sheets Physics p.58; collegedekho.com news on SREESAT-1; app notes 5:20 sub 4-5
## SUB 6 | Telecom Bodies, Spectrum and EMF Limits
[20:6:0] TABLE head: Body | Role
  [20:6:0.0] TRAI (1997) | Regulator of telecom and broadcasting
  [20:6:0.1] TDSAT (2000 amendment) | Settles disputes; hears appeals against TRAI
  [20:6:0.2] C-DOT (1984) | Government telecom R&D centre
  [20:6:0.3] TEC | DoT's technical arm: standards, equipment testing (not USOF collection)
  [20:6:0.4] DoT (1985) | Created when Posts and Telecom split; MTNL and VSNL 1986
  [20:6:0.5] ITU WTDC | World Telecommunication Development Conference, every four years
[20:6:1] - **EMF limits for towers:** India (from 1 Sept 2012) = **one-tenth of ICNIRP**: **~0.92 W/m² at 1800 MHz** (ICNIRP ~9.2 W/m²). The APPSC key 9.2 W/m² is the ICNIRP value.
[20:6:2] - **TRAI (Feb 2026):** auction across nine bands; uniform **35%** cap; new-entrant net worth **Rs 100 cr → Rs 50 cr**. **SC (Aircel, Feb 2026):** telcos **do not own spectrum**.
[20:6:3] - **Opensignal 4G speeds:** **Airtel** led 4G **download** speed (2018–20 reports); **Vodafone (Vi)** led **upload** speed.
[20:6:4] ~~ Sources: DoT EMF norms (1/10th of ICNIRP from 1 Sept 2012 – search result snippets of dot.gov.in / tarangsanchar.gov.in; 0.92 W/m² figure from app notes); thequint.com on Opensignal 2020 report (Airtel download, Vodafone upload); app notes 5:20 sub 0, 4

=== NOTES 5:22 | Ict and Governance – NeGP, Digital India Pillars, E-kranti
## SUB 0 | Digital India – Vision Areas, Nine Pillars and e-Kranti
[22:0:0] - Launched by PM Modi on **1 July 2015**; implemented/coordinated by **MeitY**; umbrella programme to make India a **digitally empowered society and knowledge economy**.
[22:0:1] # Three vision areas
[22:0:2] TABLE head: Vision area | Includes
  [22:0:2.0] Digital infrastructure as a core utility to every citizen | High-speed internet, Aadhaar identity, CSC access, cloud locker; connect villages, Wi-Fi in schools, public places, tourist centres
  [22:0:2.1] Governance and services on demand | Online/mobile services, single window, cashless transactions
  [22:0:2.2] Digital empowerment of citizens | Universal digital literacy, documents on the cloud, services in Indian languages
[22:0:3] - **NOT a key area / not an aim:** **issue of digital currency**; "digital application for export promotion"; "digital commerce and trade"; forming India's own internet companies "like China"; a framework for overseas MNCs to build data centres (UPSC 2018: **3 only**).
[22:0:4] # Nine pillars
[22:0:5] TABLE head: No. | Pillar | Flagship / data
  [22:0:5.0] 1 | Broadband Highways | BharatNet: 2,18,347 GPs (Mar 2025)
  [22:0:5.1] 2 | Universal Access to Mobile Connectivity | 4G in villages
  [22:0:5.2] 3 | Public Internet Access Programme | 5.97 lakh CSCs (Apr 2025)
  [22:0:5.3] 4 | e-Governance – reforming government through technology | e-Office
  [22:0:5.4] 5 | e-Kranti – electronic delivery of services | 44 MMPs
  [22:0:5.5] 6 | Information for All | Open Government Data platform
  [22:0:5.6] 7 | Electronics Manufacturing | Target net zero imports; Rs 2.13 lakh cr (2020-21) → Rs 5.25 lakh cr (2024-25)
  [22:0:5.7] 8 | IT for Jobs | IT skills
  [22:0:5.8] 9 | Early Harvest Programmes | Biometric attendance, Wi-Fi in universities
[22:0:6] # e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0)
[22:0:7] - Approved **2015**; **44 MMPs** (not 31); vision "**Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance**".
[22:0:8] - APPSC G1 2017: mission for **electronic delivery of all government services** = **e-Kranti**.
[22:0:9] - Principles: transformation not translation; integrated services; **cloud by default**, **mobile first** (not paper-first).
[22:0:10] - Sister missions: **Make in India (25 Sep 2014)**, **Skill India (15 Jul 2015)**.
[22:0:11] - Rural gaps: **GP fibre via BharatNet** and **4G in villages**.
[22:0:12] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 5 p.85-87; app notes 5:22 sub 4-6, 9
## SUB 1 | E-governance – Concepts, Models and Pillars
[22:1:0] - **E-governance** = use of ICT for **technology-driven governance**, aiming to **engage, enable and empower citizens**; improves **transparency**, cuts cost.
[22:1:1] - **Four pillars:** **People, Process, Technology, Resources** (MPPSC 2024).
[22:1:2] - **Gartner's four phases:** **Information → Interaction (2nd) → Transaction → Transformation (last)** (MPPSC 2025).
[22:1:3] TABLE head: Model | Example
  [22:1:3.0] G2C | Certificates, DigiLocker
  [22:1:3.1] G2B | MCA portal (MCA21), GSTN
  [22:1:3.2] G2G | NIC solutions for departments
  [22:1:3.3] G2E | Online HR tools
[22:1:4] - **MCA21** (Corporate Affairs) = **e-governance** project for companies (UPSC 2007).
[22:1:5] # Implementing bodies
[22:1:6] TABLE head: Body | Role
  [22:1:6.0] NIC (1976) | G2G solutions; built e-Taal
  [22:1:6.1] MeitY | Coordinates Digital India; UIDAI is under it
  [22:1:6.2] DeitY (now MeitY) + DARPG | Drafted NeGP
  [22:1:6.3] NeGD | MeitY's programme-management arm under Digital India Corporation; runs capacity building
  [22:1:6.4] CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd | SPV of CSCs
[22:1:7] - **Capacity building Phase III** (Sept 2024): launched by **MeitY** (NeGD with NISG) – DPI, procurement, AI/ML training for officials.
[22:1:8] - **UN EGDI 2024:** India **97th** (105th in 2022).
[22:1:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 3 p.18-19; app notes 5:22 sub 0-1, 9; indianinfrastructure.com / newsonair (MeitY Phase III, Sept 2024 – search results)
## SUB 2 | National e-Governance Plan and Mission Mode Projects
[22:2:0] - **NeGP** approved **18 May 2006**: **27 MMPs + 10 components** → 31 → **44 (e-Kranti)**; vision: services accessible to the common man **in his locality**.
[22:2:1] TABLE head: Tier | Component
  [22:2:1.0] Front end | CSCs
  [22:2:1.1] Network | SWAN
  [22:2:1.2] Back end | SDC
[22:2:2] - Others: **MSDG (2011)** – services by **mobile phone**; **MeghRaj = GI Cloud**; **india.gov.in** = National Portal.
[22:2:3] TABLE head: Category | Examples
  [22:2:3.0] Central | MCA21 (Corporate Affairs), Passport Seva (MEA), Income Tax, UID
  [22:2:3.1] State | Land Records, e-District, e-Panchayat, CCTNS
  [22:2:3.2] Integrated | eCourts, e-Procurement, CSC, e-Biz
[22:2:4] # MMPs in news
[22:2:5] TABLE head: MMP | Key fact
  [22:2:5.0] eCourts | Since 2007; Phase III 2023–27
  [22:2:5.1] CCTNS | MHA, 2009
  [22:2:5.2] IVFRT | MHA, approved 2010
  [22:2:5.3] e-Procurement | Online tenders to stop collusion
  [22:2:5.4] e-Panchayat | GS NIRNAY app (2023) records Gram Sabha decisions
[22:2:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 3 p.18-19; app notes 5:22 sub 2-3

=== NOTES 5:23 | National Policy on Information Technology – Objectives and Outcomes
## SUB 0 | NPIT 2012 – Goals, Context and Targets
[23:0:0] # Twin goals
[23:0:1] - **Goals:** bring the **full power of ICT within the reach of all** India, and make India the **Global Hub and Destination for IT and ITES Services by 2020**.
[23:0:2] - **Context (2011-12):** IT = **USD 100 bn** industry, **~80%** of revenue from **exports**; **six hubs** (Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, NCR) ≈ **90%** of the industry and near saturation.
[23:0:3] - **Spread, not concentrate:** NPIT aimed to diversify IT into **Tier II and Tier III cities** and rural areas.
[23:0:4] - **Objectives:** jobs; ICT in education, health, skills, financial inclusion, governance; Aadhaar-based authentication, PKI, payment gateways; e-governance through the NeGP.
[23:0:5] # Targets (all by 2020)
[23:0:6] TABLE head: NPIT 2012 target | Value
  [23:0:6.0] IT-ITES revenue | US$ 100 bn → US$ 300 bn
  [23:0:6.1] IT exports | US$ 69 bn → US$ 200 bn
  [23:0:6.2] Skilled manpower | 10 million more trained ICT workers
  [23:0:6.3] e-literacy | One e-literate person in every household
[23:0:7] > ⚠ Trap: NPIT 2012 deadline = **2020** (not 2025); $300 bn = revenue, $200 bn = exports.
[23:0:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 3 p.3-5; app notes 5:23 sub 1-2
## SUB 1 | IT Milestones, Institutions and Companies
[23:1:0] # Milestones
[23:1:1] TABLE head: Year | Milestone
  [23:1:1.0] 1976 | NIC set up
  [23:1:1.1] 1988 | C-DAC, Pune, set up to build the PARAM supercomputer (PARAM 8000, 1991)
  [23:1:1.2] 1998 | National Task Force on IT and Software Development
  [23:1:1.3] 2000 | IT Act, 2000: legal basis for e-records and digital signatures; amended 2008
  [23:1:1.4] 2006 | NeGP with Mission Mode Projects
  [23:1:1.5] 2009 | National e-Governance Division (NeGD) created by MeitY (then DeitY) under Media Lab Asia
  [23:1:1.6] 2012 | NPIT 2012
  [23:1:1.7] Dec 2021 | India Semiconductor Mission under MeitY
[23:1:2] # Institutions → role
[23:1:3] TABLE head: Body | Role
  [23:1:3.0] MeitY | IT, electronics, cyber-security policy
  [23:1:3.1] NIC | Government IT and e-governance network; designed and runs the National Knowledge Network (NKN)
  [23:1:3.2] NeGD | Runs UMANG, DigiLocker, Meri Pehchaan
  [23:1:3.3] NASSCOM | IT-BPM industry association
  [23:1:3.4] STPI | Export-oriented IT parks and CoEs (not the government IT network)
  [23:1:3.5] C-DAC | PARAM supercomputers, C2S programme, centre at Amaravati Quantum Valley
  [23:1:3.6] NIELIT | Deemed university under MeitY; IT and electronics training
[23:1:4] - **IT companies:** **Infosys** (co-founder and former chairman **N.R. Narayana Murthy**), **TCS**, CMC (now part of TCS); **Raymond** is a textile firm, not IT.
[23:1:5] ~~ Sources: app notes 5:23 sub 0, 5; general knowledge (NKN, NeGD 2009, Infosys, Raymond)
## SUB 2 | National Policy on Electronics 2019 and Schemes
[23:2:0] - **NPE 2019:** approved **20 February 2019**; India as a global hub for **ESDM**, **including chipsets**.
[23:2:1] TABLE head: NPE 2019 target (by 2025) | Value
  [23:2:1.0] Electronics manufacturing | US$ 400 bn (~₹26 lakh crore)
  [23:2:1.1] Mobile handsets | 1 billion a year; 600 million for export
  [23:2:1.2] Mobile manufacturing / exports | US$ 190 bn / US$ 110 bn
[23:2:2] - **Schemes (2020):** **PLI** (large-scale electronics), **SPECS** (**components and semiconductors**), **EMC 2.0** (notified **1 Apr 2020**; **electronics clusters + common facility centres**).
[23:2:3] - **MPMS** (Aug 2026): **₹62,500 crore**, FY 2026-27 to 2030-31; production **₹39 lakh crore**, exports ₹15 lakh crore; replaces **PLI (Large Scale Electronics)**.
[23:2:4] ~~ Sources: app notes 5:23 sub 3
## SUB 3 | India Semiconductor Mission
[23:3:0] - **Semicon 2.0 pillars:** **Fabs, Packaging, R&D, Design, Machines/Materials**.
[23:3:1] TABLE head: Pillar | Max support
  [23:3:1.0] CMOS silicon fabs | 40% capital subsidy
  [23:3:1.1] Compound/display fabs, advanced packaging | 35%
  [23:3:1.2] R&D | up to 75%
  [23:3:1.3] Talent | 1,00,000 engineers
[23:3:2] - **C2S (Chips to Start-up, 2022):** implemented by **C-DAC (not NIELIT)**; **85,000** students over five years.
[23:3:3] TABLE head: Unit | Company | Location
  [23:3:3.0] ATMP | Micron | Sanand, Gujarat
  [23:3:3.1] OSAT | Tata (TSAT) | Jagiroad, Assam
  [23:3:3.2] Semiconductor + OSAT | RRP Electronics | Sri Sathya Sai district, AP
[23:3:4] ~~ Sources: app notes 5:23 sub 4
## SUB 4 | Outcomes and AP IT Policy
[23:4:0] - **Digital economy:** **~12-14% of GDP**; projected **~20% by 2029-30**.
[23:4:1] - **Electronics:** production **₹13.11 lakh crore** (2025-26); electronics = **3rd-largest export** item.
[23:4:2] - **GCCs:** offshore units of MNCs serving their **own parent** (outsourcing vendors serve unrelated clients).
[23:4:3] - **AP IT & GCC Policy 4.0 (2024-29):** in force **12 Dec 2024**; AP Data Centre Policy: up to **1 GW**.
[23:4:4] - **Visakhapatnam:** **cable landing station**, AI data projects with Anakapalli, **Infosys** campus (~7,000 jobs), IoT CoE.
[23:4:5] - **Amaravati:** **Quantum Valley** (C-DAC centre), NIELIT campus.
[23:4:6] ~~ Sources: app notes 5:23 sub 6-7

=== NOTES 5:24 | E-governance Programmes and Services – Umang, Digilocker, E-sign, E-hospital, CSCs, Ap Initiatives
## SUB 0 | Andhra Pradesh Digital Governance
[24:0:0] # Service-delivery chain
[24:0:1] - **AP chain:** **e-Seva (2001) → MeeSeva (2011) → e-Pragati → RTGS → Mana Mitra (2025)**.
[24:0:2] - **e-Seva (2001):** **India's first integrated citizen service centres** (bill payments and certificates at one centre).
[24:0:3] - **MeeSeva** = "**At your service**" (Telugu): launched **4 November 2011** (Chittoor) in undivided AP – **single-window** delivery through MeeSeva centres and authorised agents (**about 11,079** in Jan 2023).
[24:0:4] - **Legal backing:** **AP IT (Electronic Service Delivery) Rules, 2011** (G.O.Ms.No.10, 18 Oct 2011) – legal sanctity to **digitally signed certificates**; departments to migrate to electronic delivery.
[24:0:5] - **Gram/Ward Sachivalayam:** launched **2 October 2019** to bring governance to the doorstep; **10,000+** secretariats, **500+** services, **SPANDANA** grievance portal.
[24:0:6] # e-Pragati and RTGS
[24:0:7] - **e-Pragati:** **whole-of-government** programme – all e-governance systems **interconnected and integrated**, free flow of information; the digital route to **'Sunrise AP 2022'**.
[24:0:8] - **Core datasets:** **People Hub, Land Hub, Entity Hub, GIS Hub, IoT Hub** (no Revenue Hub).
[24:0:9] - **RTGS (Real Time Governance Society):** **Data Lake, Data Lens, Command & Control Centre**.
[24:0:10] - **Mana Mitra (WhatsApp Governance):** AI-powered, launched **30 January 2025**; **500+** services.
[24:0:11] # Land, registration and sectoral systems
[24:0:12] TABLE head: System | Fact
  [24:0:12.0] CARD (1998) | Computer-aided Administration of Registration Department – computerised document registration
  [24:0:12.1] BhuSeva + Bhudaar | Land records online; launched 20 Nov 2018; each holding gets an 11-digit Bhudaar number
  [24:0:12.2] e-Seed (NIC-AP) | Aadhaar-enabled, webland-linked biometric distribution of subsidised groundnut seed – from Kharif 2016 (Anantapur)
  [24:0:12.3] CFST (Transport) | Online learner licence, tax tokens, transfer of ownership – not utility bills
  [24:0:12.4] Rajiv Internet Village | Aug 2004; rural kiosks run by women's self-help groups
[24:0:13] - **Not an AP project:** **e-Mitra** = Rajasthan.
[24:0:14] > Exam angle: MeeSeva year (2011) ×2, e-Pragati ×2, BhuSeva/Bhudaar ×2, "NOT an AP project" (e-Mitra).
[24:0:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 3 p.25-26, p.30; app notes 5:24 sub 3, 9; web search (MeeSeva 4 Nov 2011; AP ESD Rules 2011 text; Hans India May 2016 seed distribution)
## SUB 1 | NeGP 2006 and e-Kranti
[24:1:0] # National e-Governance Plan
[24:1:1] - **E-Governance** = use of computers/ICT in governance to deliver services – the IT-based system of governance.
[24:1:2] - Framed by **DeitY + DARPG**; approved **18 May 2006**.
[24:1:3] - **27 MMPs** (**9 Central, 11 State, 7 Integrated**) + **10 components**; later **31 MMPs**.
[24:1:4] - **Vision:** all government services **accessible to the common man in his locality** through **common service delivery outlets**, with **efficiency, transparency and reliability at affordable costs**.
[24:1:5] - **Integrated MMPs:** **e-Courts** (judiciary ICT, since **2007**), **e-Procurement**, National Portal. **State MMP:** **e-Panchayat**.
[24:1:6] - **MMP** = **Mission Mode Project**.
[24:1:7] TABLE head: Item | NeGP (1.0) | e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0)
  [24:1:7.0] MMPs | 27 → 31 | 44
  [24:1:7.1] Place | Stand-alone national plan | A pillar of Digital India
[24:1:8] > APPSC asked: approval year (2006), vision (locality, affordable cost), MMP count (27), e-Courts (2007).
[24:1:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 3 p.18-19; app notes 5:24 sub 1
## SUB 2 | Central Citizen Service Platforms
[24:2:0] TABLE head: Platform | Ministry / body | Service
  [24:2:0.0] UMANG – Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance | MeitY (NeGD), 1 Nov 2017 | One app for central, state, local services; web, SMS, IVR; 2,400+ services (Jul 2026)
  [24:2:0.1] e-Pramaan | MeitY (then DeitY); built by C-DAC | National e-Authentication framework; SAML-based single sign-on
  [24:2:0.2] Meri Pehchaan | MeitY, July 2022 | National Single Sign-On; Parichay/Jan-Parichay, e-Pramaan, DigiLocker
  [24:2:0.3] e-Office | MeitY–NIC | Paperless file management
  [24:2:0.4] MyGov | MeitY, 2014 | Citizen engagement
  [24:2:0.5] Jeevan Pramaan | MeitY, 2014 | Aadhaar-based biometric Digital Life Certificate for pensioners
  [24:2:0.6] Bhavishya | Dept of Pension & Pensioners' Welfare | Integrated pensioners' portal; Bhavishya 9.0 = base of the Integrated Pensioners' Portal (Vigyan Bhawan, 18 Oct 2022, with SBI)
  [24:2:0.7] Anubhav | Dept of Pension & Pensioners' Welfare | Online platform where retiring employees share experience
  [24:2:0.8] SARATHI / VAHAN | MoRTH | Driving licence / vehicle registration

  [24:2:0.11] Aaykar Setu | Income Tax Dept (2017) | Mobile app – online tax payment and tax tools
  [24:2:0.12] SEZ India app | Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Jan 2017 | SEZ services
  [24:2:0.13] e-Taal | NIC | Electronic Transactions Aggregation and Analysis Layer
[24:2:1] - **UMANG flaw:** Aadhaar numbers stored in plain text – forbidden by the **Aadhaar Act, 2016**.
[24:2:2] - **Technology's role in e-governance:** **enhance citizen engagement and improve service delivery** – not replacing people, cutting staff or more control.

## SUB 6 | DigiLocker, e-Sign and Secure Messaging
[24:6:0] - **DigiLocker:** **MeitY**, **February 2015** – secure personal space to **store and share digital documents**, linked to **Aadhaar**; DL and RC linked with MoRTH (Sept 2016); **56.06 crore** users.
[24:6:1] - **Legal validity:** documents = originals under **IT Act, 2000** + **Digital Locker Rules, 2016** (not the RTI Act).
[24:6:2] - **e-Sign:** **Aadhaar eKYC-based**; **PKI**, not blockchain; legal backing **IT Act, 2000**; C-DAC's **e-Hastakshar** among issuers.
[24:6:3] - **GIMS** = **Government Instant Messaging System** – government's WhatsApp alternative, released as **Sandes**; built by **NIC**.
[24:6:4] - **NIC Mail:** integrated with **CollabFiles** office suite, e-Sign, Bhashini.
[24:6:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 4 p.4; app notes 5:24 sub 5

  [24:7:2.0] G2E | CEMS (employee management)
  [24:7:2.1] G2P | DBT (LPG subsidy, pensions)
  [24:7:2.2] Open Government Data | data.gov.in
[24:7:3] # NeGP core infrastructure
[24:7:4] TABLE head: Pillar | Full form | Role
  [24:7:4.0] SWAN | State Wide Area Network | Converged backbone for data, voice, video
  [24:7:4.1] SDC | State Data Centre | Hosts state e-gov applications and data
  [24:7:4.2] CSC | Common Service Centre | Village-level front-end delivery outlet
[24:7:5] - **Not core infrastructure:** National Investment and Infrastructure Fund. **MeghRaj (GI Cloud)** now hosts government apps.
[24:7:6] - **CSCs:** SPV **CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd**; run by **Village Level Entrepreneurs**, down to **Gram Panchayats**; **400+** services.
