=== NOTES 5:25 | Digital Identity and Payments – Aadhaar, Upi, Dbt, India Stack, Ondc, Account Aggregator
## SUB 0 | Aadhaar and UIDAI
[25:0:0] # UIDAI
[25:0:1] - **UIDAI** set up **28 January 2009** as an attached office of the **Planning Commission**; statutory authority under the **Aadhaar Act, 2016**, working under **MeitY** (not Home, Finance or Rural Development).
[25:0:2] TABLE head: Act / rule / policy | Year | Provision
  [25:0:2.0] Aadhaar Act | 2016 | UIDAI made statutory under MeitY; targeted delivery of subsidies
  [25:0:2.1] Amendment | 2019 | Amended the Aadhaar Act
  [25:0:2.2] Aadhaar Authentication for Good Governance Rules | 2020 | Voluntary authentication by other entities
  [25:0:2.3] MeitY Policy on Open APIs | 2015 | Led to API Setu
[25:0:3] # Firsts
[25:0:4] TABLE head: FIRST | Fact
  [25:0:4.0] First Aadhaar number | Ranjana Sonawane, Tembhli village, Nandurbar, Maharashtra, 29 September 2010
  [25:0:4.1] Planned first issue | UIDAI planned the first set of numbers for Aug 2010 – February 2011 (exam key: February 2011)
[25:0:5] # Format and scale
[25:0:6] - **12-digit random number**, **free and lifelong**, one enrolment; no caste, religion or geography.
[25:0:7] - **Biometrics:** **10 fingerprints, 2 iris scans, face photograph**; **dactylography** = study of **fingerprints**.
[25:0:8] - **Scale:** **142 crore** numbers generated (31 Jul 2025); about 116 crore enrolled by mid-2017 (120 crore crossed only later).
[25:0:9] - **Uses:** DBT, **Jeevan Pramaan** (**digital life certificate**), e-KYC. Mobile-Aadhaar linking was mandated in 2017 but struck down by the Supreme Court in Sept 2018.
[25:0:10] - **ABHA** = **14** digits (health ID), Aadhaar = 12.
[25:0:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 4 p.3; app notes 5:25 sub 1-2; general knowledge (dactylography, 2017 enrolment, 2018 judgment)
## SUB 1 | UPI, NPCI Products and Payment Systems
[25:1:0] # UPI
[25:1:1] - Launched **April 2016** by **NPCI**; one app, several bank accounts, **VPA**.
[25:1:2] - **UPI 2.0:** daily limit **Rs 2 lakh**; **UPI Lite:** on-device wallet **without a UPI PIN**.
[25:1:3] - **Abroad:** **France** = **first country in Europe** to accept UPI (Feb 2024); **PayNow-UPI** link with **Singapore** (2023).
[25:1:4] TABLE head: Product | Key fact
  [25:1:4.0] BHIM | NPCI's UPI app; 30 December 2016
  [25:1:4.1] e-RUPI | One-time, cashless, person- and purpose-specific voucher; NPCI with DFS, MoHFW, NHA; launched by PM Modi, August 2021
  [25:1:4.2] Vajra | NPCI platform for fast and secure payments (DLT-based clearing)
  [25:1:4.3] NFS | National Financial Switch – links all ATMs; built by IDRBT (2004), now run by NPCI
[25:1:5] # Operators
[25:1:6] TABLE head: System | Operator
  [25:1:6.0] NEFT, RTGS | RBI
  [25:1:6.1] IMPS, UPI, AePS, BBPS, NACH, RuPay | NPCI
  [25:1:6.2] FASTag (NETC) | NPCI with NHAI/IHMCL
  [25:1:6.3] iPay gateway | IRCTC
[25:1:7] - **AePS** = cash withdrawal and balance enquiry at micro-ATMs using Aadhaar.
[25:1:8] - **New Umbrella Entities:** RBI move to end NPCI's monopoly; minimum capital **Rs 500 crore**.
[25:1:9] - **First digital (mobile) wallet company:** **MobiKwik** (2009).
[25:1:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 4 p.1; app notes 5:25 sub 3-4; web search (MobiKwik 2009)
## SUB 2 | Nodal Bodies, Committees and Digitisation Drive
[25:2:0] - **After demonetisation (Nov 2016):** **NITI Aayog** coordinated the drive to make **100% Government-Citizen transactions digital**; **Committee of Chief Ministers on Digitisation** headed by **N. Chandrababu Naidu**.
[25:2:1] - **MeitY** got "Promotion of Digital Transactions" in **February 2017** (taken over from NITI Aayog).
[25:2:2] - **17 July 2023:** "Promotion of Digital Payments" moved to the **Department of Financial Services (Ministry of Finance)** – the present nodal body.
[25:2:3] - **Nilekani Committee:** set up by **RBI in January 2019** on deepening digital payments.
[25:2:4] - **RBI Digital Payments Index:** base **March 2018 = 100**; published **half-yearly**.
[25:2:5] ~~ Sources: app notes 5:25 sub 5; general knowledge (NITI Aayog 2016, Naidu committee, Nilekani 2019)
## SUB 3 | India Stack and Open Digital Platforms
[25:3:0] TABLE head: India Stack layer | Component
  [25:3:0.0] Identity (presence-less) | Aadhaar, e-KYC
  [25:3:0.1] Cashless | UPI
  [25:3:0.2] Paperless | eSign, DigiLocker
  [25:3:0.3] Consent | DEPA / Account Aggregator
[25:3:1] - India Stack gives **online, paperless, cashless** access and cuts e-KYC cost – through the **identity layer (Aadhaar e-KYC)**, not the payments layer; the original stack had 3 layers, consent was added later.
[25:3:2] - **Open-source platforms:** **Aarogya Setu, CoWIN, DigiLocker, DIKSHA** – all four (UPSC 2022).
[25:3:3] - **ONDC (2022):** open e-commerce network that **breaks platform monopolies**.
[25:3:4] - **Account Aggregator:** consent-based sharing of financial data (not the identity layer).
[25:3:5] - Digital economy: **12-14% of GDP**.
[25:3:6] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 5 p.77-80; app notes 5:25 sub 0
## SUB 4 | DBT – JAM and Delivery in Andhra Pradesh
[25:4:0] - **JAM** = Jan Dhan + Aadhaar + Mobile; DBT routed via **CPSMS (now PFMS)** + NPCI's **Aadhaar Payment Bridge**.
[25:4:1] - **First JAM application:** **PAHAL** (LPG subsidy). **DBT Mission:** now in the **Cabinet Secretariat**.
[25:4:2] - **Numbers:** **Rs 44 lakh crore** transferred (May 2025); savings **Rs 3.48 lakh crore** (2015 to Mar 2023); **PMJDY 58.77 crore** accounts (Aug 2026), **more than half held by women**.
[25:4:3] - **AP:** DBT inaugurated at **Gollaprolu, East Godavari**, **6 January 2013** by **Jairam Ramesh**; Aadhaar e-PoS PDS from **Krishna** (May 2015); AP = first state with **e-PoS in 100% of fair price shops**.
[25:4:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 4 p.4; app notes 5:25 sub 7-8

## SUB 0 | BharatNet and Rural Connectivity
[26:0:0] TABLE head: Date | Event
  [26:0:0.0] 25 Oct 2011 | NOFN approved for 2.5 lakh gram panchayats
  [26:0:0.1] 25 Feb 2012 | BBNL (SPV) registered
  [26:0:0.2] Feb 2023 | BBNL merged with BSNL
  [26:0:0.3] 22 Feb 2026 | AP MoC with the Digital Bharat Nidhi Administrator: 13,426 village panchayats
[26:0:1] - **BBNL mission:** broadband up to **100 Mbps per GP**, scalable to **1 Gbps**; laid using fibre of **BSNL, RailTel, PGCIL**; funded by USOF; GPON technology.
[26:0:2] - **Phase III / Amended BharatNet:** **Rs 1.39 lakh crore**; **PPP**; AP SPV = **AP BharatNet Infrastructure Ltd**.
[26:0:3] - **APSWAN** = **Andhra Pradesh State Wide Area Network**; **AP FiberNet** reached 4,000+ tribal hamlets (**Eastern Ghats**).
[26:0:4] - **USOF:** **non-lapsable** fund for commercially unviable rural telecom; renamed **Digital Bharat Nidhi** (Telecommunications Act 2023). LWE Phase I 2G sites set up by **BSNL**.

## SUB 1 | Digital Literacy – PMGDISHA and Schools
[26:1:0] - **NDLM** and **DISHA** (**Digital Saksharta Abhiyan**) preceded **PMGDISHA**.
[26:1:1] - **PMGDISHA:** launched at **Gandhinagar**; **rural**; **6 crore households**, one person each; age **14-60**; closed 31 March 2024 with **4.78 crore** certified.
[26:1:2] TABLE head: Scheme | Focus
  [26:1:2.0] Vidya Vahini | Computer education in government schools
  [26:1:2.1] ICT@Schools | Computer labs in government schools

=== NOTES 5:27 | Ict in Andhra Pradesh – E-pragati, Rtgs, Mee Seva and State Digital Initiatives
## SUB 0 | MeeSeva and e-Seva – Single-window Citizen Services
[27:0:0] # Journey
[27:0:1] - **AP's e-governance legacy:** **N. Chandrababu Naidu's SMART governance** model and the **HITEC City** IT push of 1995-2004 – "**use of IT for development**" was the stated strategy of the **Andhra Pradesh Government** (UPPSC 1998).
[27:0:2] - **e-Seva** began in **2001**; it was succeeded by **MeeSeva** in **2011** (combined state) as the **single-window G2C** delivery mechanism.
[27:0:3] - **"MeeSeva"** in Telugu = **"At your service"**; channels: **MeeSeva franchise centres** + **online portal**; also enrolment for Aarogya Raksha.
[27:0:4] # Service categories
[27:0:5] TABLE head: Category | Meaning
  [27:0:5.0] Category A | Over-the-counter services issued on the spot (e.g. certified copies)
  [27:0:5.1] Category B | Statutory services needing notices, hearings or field verification (departmental workflow)
[27:0:6] # Departments inside MeeSeva
[27:0:7] TABLE head: Department | Role
  [27:0:7.0] EDS Department | Prints MeeSeva certificates
  [27:0:7.1] Education Department | Migration certificates (passed candidates only)
[27:0:8] # Other AP registration and portal services
[27:0:9] TABLE head: AP project | Department / service
  [27:0:9.0] CARD (Computer-aided Administration of Registration Department) | Registration Department: computer-aided registration of property documents (not revenue land records)
  [27:0:9.1] AP Online | Web portal for G2C services
  [27:0:9.2] Registration Service Kendras (2026) | Property registration on the Passport Seva Kendra model; legal powers stay with Sub-Registrar Offices
[27:0:10] - **RSK debate:** effect on **document writers'** livelihoods; State assures SROs are **not being privatised**.
[27:0:11] - **Telangana pairs (APPSC Sample Taker):** **T Wallet** – Telangana's official e-wallet, launched **1 June 2017**; **DOST** (Degree Online Services Telangana) – online degree admissions; DOST itself began in **2016**, the **DOST-2021** cycle opened **1 July 2021** (the key reads pair II this way).
[27:0:12] > APPSC 2023: MeeSeva = "At your service"; EDS prints certificates; Education Dept issues migration certificates – all pairs correct. Category B = statutory (notices/hearings/field inspection).
[27:0:13] ~~ Sources: app notes 5:27 sub 0-1; NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 3 p.26 (CARD); web: thenewsminute.com (T-Wallet 1 Jun 2017), en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Degree_Online_Services_Telangana (DOST 2016)
## SUB 1 | e-Pragati, APSWAN and AP FiberNet
[27:1:0] # e-Pragati – AP State Enterprise Architecture
[27:1:1] - **e-Pragati** = new name of the **AP State Enterprise Architecture (APSEA)**: comprehensive, **whole-of-government** e-governance – all e-Governance systems interconnected; core datasets **People Hub, Land Hub, Entity Hub, GIS Hub, IoT Hub**.
[27:1:2] - Introduced under CM **Chandrababu Naidu**; approved by the state cabinet in **2015**.
[27:1:3] - Outlay **Rs 2,358 crore**: **72 projects** in **14 packages**, over three years; state share about Rs 1,528 crore, rest via **PPP**; covers **33 secretariat departments** and **300+ agencies**; built with **Wipro**.
[27:1:4] # APSWAN and networks
[27:1:5] - **APSWAN** (AP State Wide Area Network) = backbone network linking the **state capital (Secretariat), district HQs and mandal HQs** under **NeGP**; operational **Nov 2010**; initial capacity **2 Mbps**.
[27:1:6] - Upgraded to **APSDWAN** (software-defined) on **1 May 2021**; DHQ–MHQ links 8 Mbps; **APSCAN** (Secretariat campus, Velagapudi, 2016); AP State Data Centre at Pi Data Centers, Mangalagiri.
[27:1:7] # AP FiberNet
[27:1:8] - **AP State FiberNet Ltd (APSFL):** incorporated **October 2015** under the Companies Act 2013; under the Energy, Infrastructure & Investment Dept; runs the **AP Fibergrid** – inaugurated by the **President** in **December 2017**.
[27:1:9] - **Triple-play**: **broadband + TV + telephone**; basic plan **Rs 149** (15 Mbps, ~250 TV channels); reached **4,000+ tribal hamlets** in the Eastern Ghats.
[27:1:10] > e-Pragati (not Citi Net / e-Jan Seva) = the comprehensive AP e-governance project; APSWAN (not APSLAN/APSMAN) links capital–districts–mandals.
[27:1:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 3 p.30 (e-Pragati, APSFL); AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 p.169-170 (APSWAN, APSDWAN, APSCAN); app notes 5:27 sub 2, 7

## SUB 3 | RTGS and Mana Mitra
[27:3:0] # Real Time Governance Society
[27:3:1] - **RTGS** formed on **6 September 2017**; works directly under the **Chief Minister**; **RTG State Centre** (command centre) inaugurated at the **Secretariat, Velagapudi** on **26 November 2017**.
[27:3:2] - Dashboards pull data from surveillance cameras, drones, biometric systems and **AWARE** (AP Weather Forecasting and Early Warning Research Centre).
[27:3:3] - Revived from **2024** as an **AI-driven** governance platform; **Swarna Andhra @2047** pillar "**Effective Governance and AI-based Public Services**"; AP has **59 Chief Data Officers**.
[27:3:4] # Mana Mitra – WhatsApp governance
[27:3:5] - Launched **30 January 2025**; run by **RTGS**.
[27:3:6] TABLE head: Stage | Data
  [27:3:6.0] Launch (Jan 2025) | 150 services
  [27:3:6.1] 2025-26 | 865 services
  [27:3:6.2] Cap per service | 5 user inputs, 2 documents
[27:3:7] - Services: **rice card eKYC, electricity bills, 1-B Adangal, APSRTC tickets, TTD and temple darshan**.
[27:3:8] - Temples: **Rs 22.26 crore** to **21 temples**; top earner = **Srikalahasti** (not Tirumala).
[27:3:9] ~~ Sources: app notes 5:27 sub 3
## SUB 4 | Rajiv Internet Village (RAJiv)
[27:4:0] - **RAJiv** launched by CM **Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy** in **August 2004** to bring **government services closer to rural people** (affordable, transparent).
[27:4:1] - First internet village: **Chiluvuru** (Duggirala mandal, Guntur district).
[27:4:2] - Village kiosks run by local entrepreneurs: **utility bill payment**, state **bus tickets**, land records; contract with **Bharat Electronics** (Dec 2004) for **5,550** centres in 14 districts.
[27:4:3] ~~ Sources: web: business-standard.com (launch Aug 2004), en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiluvuru (first internet village); app notes 5:27 sub 6

=== NOTES 5:28 | Netiquettes – Digital Etiquette, Digital Literacy, Misinformation and Fake News
## SUB 0 | Online Safety Practices and Helplines
[28:0:0] # Recommended vs NOT recommended
[28:0:1] TABLE head: Recommended | NOT recommended
  [28:0:1.0] Strong passwords | Accepting friend requests from unknown people without caution
  [28:0:1.1] Multi-factor / two-factor authentication | Clicking a link or scanning a QR code to receive money
  [28:0:1.2] Verifying information before sharing | Paying a "friend" who urgently asks for money without checking
  [28:0:1.3] Caution with personal/sensitive data; privacy settings | Open, unsecured Wi-Fi
  [28:0:1.4] WPA3 Wi-Fi; keep digital footprint low | Sharing OTPs
[28:0:2] - Friend urgently asks for money: verify through **another channel** (ID may be hacked).
[28:0:3] - Report cyber offences: **cybercrime.gov.in** and helpline **1930**.
[28:0:4] # Campaigns
[28:0:5] TABLE head: Campaign | Fact
  [28:0:5.0] Stay Safe Online | MeitY (Ashwini Vaishnaw), December 2022, under India's G20 presidency – online-safety awareness
  [28:0:5.1] Stay Safe with WhatsApp | April 2023, a three-month campaign (not 30 days): Block and Report, Two-Step Verification, privacy and group settings
  [28:0:5.2] #OnlineButUnafraid | Telangana Cyber Security Bureau cyber-hygiene campaign (20 Mar 2026)
[28:0:6] # Helplines
[28:0:7] TABLE head: Number | Purpose
  [28:0:7.0] 1098 | Childline – Ministry of Women & Child Development
  [28:0:7.1] 1075 | National health helpline – MoHFW
  [28:0:7.2] 14567 | Senior citizens (Elderline) – M/o Social Justice
  [28:0:7.3] 080-46110007 | NIMHANS psychological support
  [28:0:7.4] 1930 | Cyber financial fraud
[28:0:8] > "Which is NOT a safe practice?" = accepting friend requests from unknown persons.

## SUB 1 | Digital Literacy and Computer Literacy Day
[28:1:0] - **Computer Literacy Day / World Computer Literacy Day:** **2 December** – started by **NIIT** in **2001** (its 20th anniversary); spreads computer skills, especially among women and children.
[28:1:1] - Digital India **Vision Area 3** (Digital Empowerment of Citizens) begins with **Universal Digital Literacy**.
[28:1:2] TABLE head: Scheme | Feature
  [28:1:2.0] PMGDISHA | One digitally literate person in each rural family; launched by PM at Gandhinagar
  [28:1:2.1] ULLAS | 2022-27, Ministry of Education (not MeitY), adults 15+; digital + financial literacy
[28:1:3] - NSS CAMS 2022-23 (age 15-24): **78.4%** could send e-mail with attachment; 71.2% could copy-paste.
[28:1:4] - **Himachal Pradesh** = 5th State/UT with full functional literacy.
[28:1:5] - Other days: **21 March** Universal Acceptance Day; **1 July** Digital India anniversary; 10 Dec Human Rights Day.
[28:1:6] ~~ Sources: app notes 5:28 sub 7
## SUB 2 | Netiquette and Online Behaviour Terms
[28:2:0] # Netiquette
[28:2:1] - **Netiquette** = the **Internet's ethical protocol** (net + etiquette); **etiquette** = the customary code of polite behaviour in a social group.
[28:2:2] - Core rule: **constructive online dialogue** and **respect privacy**; "**digital freedom** should be accompanied by **digital responsibility**".
[28:2:3] TABLE head: Medium | Do | Don't
  [28:2:3.0] Email | Clear subject line, polite greeting, check recipients | Type in ALL CAPS (reads as shouting); forward chain mails
  [28:2:3.1] Social media | Verify before sharing, respect privacy, credit sources | Post others' photos without consent (even if credited); troll
  [28:2:3.2] Online meetings | Join on time, mute when not speaking | Talk over others; record without permission
  [28:2:3.3] Online forums | Stay on topic, civil discourse | Trolling, spamming
[28:2:4] # Terms
[28:2:5] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [28:2:5.0] Cyber venting | Using websites to pour out one's grievances (e.g. against employer)
  [28:2:5.1] Nomophobia | Irrational fear of being without one's mobile (no signal, low battery, no balance)
  [28:2:5.2] Trolling | Deliberately provocative or abusive content
  [28:2:5.3] Cyberbullying | Repeated online harassment, esp. of children
  [28:2:5.4] Doxxing | Publicly sharing someone's private info without consent; no universal legal definition; prosecuted under stalking/harassment/cyber laws
  [28:2:5.5] Cyberstalking | Repeated unwanted monitoring or contact online
  [28:2:5.6] Digital footprint | Trail of data a person leaves online
  [28:2:5.7] Filter bubble | Algorithms rank content by user preference, isolating users
[28:2:6] # Sections → offence
[28:2:7] TABLE head: Section | Offence
  [28:2:7.0] IT Act 66E | Privacy violation
  [28:2:7.1] IT Act 67 | Obscene material
  [28:2:7.2] BNS 78 | Stalking, incl. monitoring electronic communication
[28:2:8] ~~ Sources: app notes 5:28 sub 0, 2; general knowledge (netiquette, etiquette, not checked)
## SUB 3 | Misinformation, Fact-checks and Critical Thinking
[28:3:0] TABLE head: Type | Meaning
  [28:3:0.0] Misinformation | False content, no intent to deceive
  [28:3:0.1] Disinformation | False content deliberately created for political/social/economic goals
  [28:3:0.2] Malinformation | Genuine information shared to cause harm (leaked private data)
[28:3:1] - Echo chambers / filter bubbles strengthen fake news; **deepfakes** = AI-made fake audio/video.
[28:3:2] - **Critical thinking** = determining the **quality of our beliefs** (evidence, reasoning) – not speed, memory or brainstorming; **NEP 2020** stresses **critical thinking and civic engagement** as an answer to fake news.
[28:3:3] # Fact-check timeline
[28:3:4] TABLE head: Date | Event
  [28:3:4.0] Nov 2019 | PIB Fact Check Unit set up – debunks fake news about Government of India, ministries, PSUs
  [28:3:4.1] 2021 | IT (Intermediary Guidelines & Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules under Sec. 87; SSMIs file monthly compliance reports
  [28:3:4.2] April 2023 | Amendment: intermediary loses safe harbour if content on Central Government business is flagged "fake" by PIB FCU

=== NOTES 5:29 | Cyber Security Concerns – Cyber Crime Types, Malware, Ransomware, Phishing, Social Engineering
## SUB 0 | Malware – Virus, Worm, Trojan and Other Types
[29:0:0] # Basics
[29:0:1] - **Malware** (malicious software) = single word for viruses, worms, trojans etc.: software **designed to disrupt, damage or gain unauthorised access** to a computer (not merely buggy software).
[29:0:2] - **VIRUS** = "**Vital Information Resources Under Siege**"; a program that **replicates itself**, **attaches to files** and spreads from computer to computer – enters via **images, audio/video files, downloads, attachments**; infects storage such as a **pen drive**, not a display or keyboard.
[29:0:3] - **Bug** = a fault in a program that stops it working correctly (some GK keys also call a virus a "bug").
[29:0:4] - **Father of computer virology:** **John von Neumann** (1949 theory of self-reproducing automata).
[29:0:5] # Types → behaviour → example
[29:0:6] TABLE head: Type | Defining behaviour | Example
  [29:0:6.0] Virus | Attaches to files, reproduces and spreads; user must run the infected file | Brain, Michelangelo
  [29:0:6.1] Worm | Uses the network to send copies of itself without user action; does not need to attach to a program | WannaCry, Morris
  [29:0:6.2] Trojan | Looks like legitimate software, tricks the user into installing it, then acts like a virus/worm; no self-replication; backdoor | Zeus
  [29:0:6.3] Ransomware | Encrypts files, demands ransom (often crypto) | WannaCry, Petya
  [29:0:6.4] Spyware | Secret surveillance; steals passwords, banking data | Pegasus
  [29:0:6.5] Adware | Unwanted ads; bundled with free/pirated software | Fireball
  [29:0:6.6] Rootkit | Administrator-level access; modifies the host OS to hide malware; hardest to detect | Stuxnet parts
  [29:0:6.7] Stealth virus | Designed to hide from antivirus detection | –
  [29:0:6.8] Keylogger | Records keystrokes (passwords, PINs, OTPs) | DarkHotel
  [29:0:6.9] Botnet | Network of hijacked "zombie" devices for DDoS, spam | Mirai (IoT)
[29:0:7] - **Antivirus** software: McAfee, Kaspersky, Avast, **Webroot**, Norton – **Rootkit is malware, not antivirus**; Webroot is not a virus.
[29:0:8] - Viruses, worms and trojans all threaten **electronic payment systems**.
[29:0:9] > "Self-replicating over the network without user action" = worm; "disguised, no self-replication" = trojan. UPSC 2005: worm statement I correct, II (needs to attach) wrong; malware statement II correct only.
[29:0:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 3 p.22 (cyber security, anti-virus); PMF S&T Part 6 p.18-20 (malware types table); app notes 5:29 sub 0; general knowledge (stealth virus, von Neumann, Webroot, not checked)
## SUB 1 | Named Malware, Attacks and Firsts
[29:1:0] TABLE head: Name | Type | Origin / note
  [29:1:0.0] Creeper (1971) | First self-copying program/virus | ARPANET (Bob Thomas, BBN); removed by Reaper
  [29:1:0.1] Elk Cloner (1982) | First virus "in the wild" | Apple II, Rich Skrenta
  [29:1:0.2] Brain (1986) | First IBM-PC boot-sector virus | Alvi brothers, Lahore, Pakistan
  [29:1:0.3] Michelangelo | Virus | Made to infect MS-DOS on 6 March 1992; first found in Australia (1991)
  [29:1:0.4] Stuxnet (2010) | Worm with rootkit parts | Sabotaged uranium centrifuges at Natanz, Iran (industrial control systems)
  [29:1:0.5] Petya (2016) / NotPetya (June 2017) | Ransomware | Encrypts the master boot record; NotPetya hit Ukraine
  [29:1:0.6] WannaCry (May 2017) | Ransomware spreading as a worm | Paralysed networks in 150 countries; used EternalBlue; Lazarus group (North Korea)
  [29:1:0.7] EternalBlue | Exploit of a Windows SMB flaw | US NSA; leaked by Shadow Brokers (2017)
  [29:1:0.8] StrandHogg (2019) | Android vulnerability | Malware poses as genuine apps; MHA alert; found by Promon (Norway)
  [29:1:0.9] Pegasus | Zero-click spyware | NSO Group, Israel
  [29:1:0.10] Mirai | Botnet | Hijacked IoT devices for DDoS
[29:1:1] - CERT-In flags (2014): Hikti, Dyreza Trojan, Shellshock.
[29:1:2] > UPSC 2018 / APPSC G2 2025: WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue = **cyber attacks / ransomware**. "Latest" virus in a 2017 paper = Petya (now many later ransomware strains).
[29:1:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 3 p.7 (CERT-In 2014 malware); PMF S&T Part 6 p.20 (UPSC 2018 WannaCry/Petya/EternalBlue = cyber attacks); app notes 5:29 sub 1
## SUB 2 | Attack Techniques – Phishing, Spoofing, Spam, DoS
[29:2:0] TABLE head: Threat | Meaning
  [29:2:0.0] Phishing | Deceptive e-mails/texts that look legitimate, tricking users into revealing sensitive information (card details, PIN) or installing software
  [29:2:0.1] Vishing | Phishing by voice calls
  [29:2:0.2] Spoofing | E-mail appears to come from one source but is sent from another; a fake website posing as a legitimate one steals user data
  [29:2:0.3] Spam | Junk / unsolicited bulk e-mail (a computer term)
  [29:2:0.4] E-mail bombing | Identical e-mail sent repeatedly to one address to overflow it
  [29:2:0.5] Sniffing | Capturing data packets on a network
  [29:2:0.6] DoS / DDoS | Denial of Service: flooding a server with fake traffic so genuine users cannot access it; DDoS uses many machines (botnet)
  [29:2:0.7] Man-in-the-middle | Secretly intercepts/alters communication between two parties
  [29:2:0.8] SQL injection | Malicious database code via website input fields
  [29:2:0.9] Zero-day | Exploits an unknown, unpatched flaw (e.g. Pegasus)
  [29:2:0.10] Supply-chain attack | Compromise a trusted vendor, e.g. SolarWinds (2020)
  [29:2:0.11] Social engineering | Exploiting the human element (trust, urgency, curiosity) to gain access
[29:2:1] - **Cyber attack** = any attempt to harm, damage or threaten a computer system or network.
[29:2:2] > Match (APPSC): Hacking – unauthorised access/manipulation; Phishing – fraudulent attempt to get sensitive info; Ransomware – locks data and demands payment.
[29:2:3] ~~ Sources: app notes 5:29 sub 2; PMF S&T Part 6 p.20-21 (phishing, vishing, DoS/DDoS); general knowledge (sniffing, not checked)
## SUB 3 | Hackers and Cyber Crimes
[29:3:0] - **Cybercrime** = any crime involving a computer and a network: **hacking, stalking, DoS attacks**, spam, online fraud, cyber terrorism (**online chatting is not a cybercrime**); deviant acts through IT = **cyber crimes**.
[29:3:1] TABLE head: Actor | Meaning
  [29:3:1.0] Hacker | Person who gains illegal/unauthorised access to a computer system
  [29:3:1.1] Cracker = black-hat hacker | Malicious hacker: destroys data, denies service
  [29:3:1.2] White-hat hacker | Ethical hacker
[29:3:2] # Crimes against persons
[29:3:3] TABLE head: Crime | Modus operandi / law
  [29:3:3.0] Digital arrest | Not a real police power – a term used by cyber criminals to scare victims: posing as police/CBI on video call and extorting money

## SUB 4 | Security Tools, Principles and Cryptography
[29:4:0] # Tools
[29:4:1] TABLE head: Tool | Function
  [29:4:1.0] Firewall | Filters incoming/outgoing internet traffic by rules; blocks unauthorised access; hardware, software or both
  [29:4:1.1] Antivirus | Prevents and heals infections
  [29:4:1.2] Password | Improves security
  [29:4:1.3] MFA / 2FA | Password + OTP/biometric
  [29:4:1.4] Honeypot | Decoy system to trap attackers
  [29:4:1.5] Virtual keyboard | Defeats keyloggers: protects against password theft, trojans and spyware
[29:4:2] - Indigenous: **M-Kavach** = **C-DAC Hyderabad**; **CERT-In** = CVE Numbering Authority.
[29:4:3] # CIA triad
[29:4:4] TABLE head: Principle | Meaning
  [29:4:4.0] Confidentiality | Procedures, policies and controls securing data against illicit access or use
  [29:4:4.1] Integrity | Protection against alteration
  [29:4:4.2] Availability | Access for authorised users (denial = availability lost)
[29:4:5] - Full list: confidentiality, integrity, availability, **accountability, non-repudiation**; **IRDAI** (2021) retail cyber cover excludes **gross negligence**.
[29:4:6] # Cryptography
[29:4:7] TABLE head: Term | Key point
  [29:4:7.0] Symmetric | Same key encrypts and decrypts – AES, Blowfish (Bruce Schneier, 1993; faster alternative to DES)
  [29:4:7.1] Asymmetric | Public-private key pair – RSA; basis of PKI
  [29:4:7.2] Digital signature | Signed with sender's private key, verified with public key
  [29:4:7.3] Hashing | One-way, fixed-length digest (SHA-256)
[29:4:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 3 p.22 (firewalls, encryption, passwords); app notes 5:29 sub 5-7

=== NOTES 5:33 | Evolution of the Indian Space Programme - Incospar, Vikram Sarabhai, Key Milestones
## SUB 0 | First Satellites and Early Experiments (1975-1988)
[33:0:0] # Aryabhata – India's first satellite
[33:0:1] - **First Indian satellite:** **Aryabhata**, launched **19 April 1975**; with it India **entered the space age** (asked 9 times: "first satellite", "1975", "19 April 1975", "first satellite experiment").
[33:0:2] - **Launch:** by the **Soviet Union** on a **Kosmos-3M** rocket from **Kapustin Yar** (USSR), not from Sriharikota; weight **360 kg**.
[33:0:3] - **Named after** the 5th-century astronomer Aryabhata; **conceived by Sarabhai**, launched after his death; satellite team led by **U.R. Rao**.
[33:0:4] # Early satellites and experiments
[33:0:5] TABLE head: Date | Satellite / experiment | Vehicle / site
  [33:0:5.0] 1 Aug 1975-76 | SITE (Satellite Instructional Television Experiment): first use of space technology for education; ~2,400 villages, ~5 million people | NASA's ATS-6 satellite
  [33:0:5.1] 19 Apr 1975 | Aryabhata: first Indian satellite, 360 kg | Soviet Kosmos-3M, Kapustin Yar
  [33:0:5.2] 1977-79 | STEP (Satellite Telecommunication Experiments Project) | Franco-German Symphonie satellite
  [33:0:5.3] 1979-81 | Bhaskara I (1979) and II: experimental earth observation | Soviet Intercosmos rocket, Baikonur
  [33:0:5.4] 18 Jul 1980 | Rohini (RS-1): first satellite on an Indian-made rocket; India the 6th nation to do so | SLV-3, Sriharikota (AP)
  [33:0:5.5] 19 Jun 1981 | APPLE (Ariane Passenger Payload Experiment): first experimental geostationary communication satellite | Ariane-1, Kourou, French Guiana
  [33:0:5.6] 1983 | INSAT-1B (INSAT system operational) | US Space Shuttle Challenger
  [33:0:5.7] 1988 | IRS-1A: first operational remote-sensing satellite | Soviet Vostok, Baikonur
[33:0:6] - **Chronology of programmes:** **SITE (1975) → STEP (1977) → APPLE (1981) → IGMDP (1983)**: code **D, C, A, B** (UPPCS 1998).
[33:0:7] - **Chronology of satellites:** **Aryabhata (1975) → Bhaskara I (1979) → Rohini (1980) → APPLE (1981)**.
[33:0:8] > ⚠ Trap: ATS-6 (NASA) served **SITE**, not APPLE; APPLE went up on Ariane-1. Bhaskara, Apple, Rohini, Agni are "first satellite" distractors (Agni is a missile).
[33:0:9] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.98-100 (book p.81-83); NextGen S&T G2 Part 2 p.6-7 (SLV-3/Rohini); app notes 5:33 (sub 1)
## SUB 1 | Vikram Sarabhai and ISRO Chairmen
[33:1:0] # Vikram Sarabhai (1919-71)
[33:1:1] - **Father of the Indian Space Programme** (not Bhabha, Kalam, Dhawan or C.V. Raman); chaired **INCOSPAR** (1962); set up **TERLS**; **first ISRO Chairman** till his death in **1971**.
[33:1:2] - **Padma Bhushan 1966**; **Padma Vibhushan posthumously 1972**; succeeded **Homi Bhabha** at the Atomic Energy Commission (**1966**).
[33:1:3] - **COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal** (since 1990): 2026 winner **Annapurni Subramaniam** – 4th Indian, first Indian woman.
[33:1:4] # Chairmen in order
[33:1:5] TABLE head: Chairman | Tenure | Highlight
  [33:1:5.0] Vikram Sarabhai | 1969-71 | First Chairman; TERLS, SITE planned
  [33:1:5.1] Satish Dhawan | 1972-84 | Aryabhata, Bhaskara, SLV-3/Rohini, APPLE
  [33:1:5.2] U.R. Rao | 1984-94 | ASLV, PSLV development, IRS-1A; Padma Vibhushan 2017
  [33:1:5.3] K. Kasturirangan | 1994-2003 | PSLV operational (1994), GSLV first flight
  [33:1:5.4] G. Madhavan Nair | 2003-09 | Chandrayaan-1 (answer for papers of 2003-09)
  [33:1:5.5] K. Radhakrishnan | 31 Oct 2009-2014 | Mangalyaan (answer for 2010-14 papers)
  [33:1:5.6] A.S. Kiran Kumar | Jan 2015-Jan 2018 | 104-satellite PSLV launch (2017) (answer for 2015-17 papers)
  [33:1:5.7] K. Sivan | 15 Jan 2018-Jan 2022 | Chandrayaan-2 (July 2019), Mission Shakti
  [33:1:5.8] S. Somanath | 14 Jan 2022-Jan 2025 | Chandrayaan-3, Aditya-L1, SpaDeX
  [33:1:5.9] V. Narayanan | from 14 Jan 2025 (in office Sep 2026) | 11th Chairman; former LPSC director
[33:1:6] - **Heads in 2011:** ISRO – V.K. Saraswat ✗ (Saraswat headed **DRDO**); **VSSC – P.S. Veeraraghavan** ✓ (Director 2010-13); DRDO – Radhakrishnan ✗ (he headed ISRO) → "only b" (Degree Lecturers 2011).
[33:1:7] - **Padma Vibhushan 2017:** **U.R. Rao** (Kasturirangan got it in 2000, Madhavan Nair in 2009; Kiran Kumar has the Padma Shri).
[33:1:8] > ⚠ Chairman questions are dated: answer by the paper's year (2008 → Madhavan Nair; 2010 → Radhakrishnan; 2017 → Kiran Kumar; 2018-21 → Sivan). Shailesh Nayak held only a short interim charge (2015).
[33:1:9] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.37 (Sarabhai), p.39 (Sivan 2018-22); Praveen CA360 Sep 2026 magazine p.81 (Chairman V. Narayanan); app notes 5:33 (sub 3), 5:34 (sub 1); general knowledge for Padma years and Veeraraghavan (not checked)
## SUB 2 | Institutional Beginnings – INCOSPAR, ISRO, DoS, TERLS
[33:2:0] # INCOSPAR, ISRO, Department of Space
[33:2:1] TABLE head: Body | Year | Fact
  [33:2:1.0] INCOSPAR (Indian National Committee for Space Research) | 1962 | Under the Department of Atomic Energy; set up with Homi Bhabha, led by Vikram Sarabhai
  [33:2:1.1] ISRO | 15 Aug 1969 | Superseded INCOSPAR (not 1967, 1970 or 1974)
  [33:2:1.2] Department of Space + Space Commission | 1972 (1 June) | ISRO brought under DoS; DoS reports to the PM
[33:2:2] - INCOSPAR (1962) came first; ISRO (1969) replaced it; DoS and Space Commission came in 1972.
[33:2:3] # TERLS, Thumba
[33:2:4] - **Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station**, Thumba, Thiruvananthapuram (**Kerala**) – not UP, Bihar or Jharkhand; chosen because it lies close to the **magnetic equator** (equatorial electrojet studies); sounding rockets only, no satellites.
[33:2:5] - First sounding rocket: **Nike-Apache** (American-built), **21 Nov 1963**.
[33:2:6] - **RH-75**: first **Indian-made** sounding rocket, **20 Nov 1967**.
[33:2:7] - Satellite Telecommunication Earth Station, **Ahmedabad**: **1 Jan 1967**.
[33:2:8] > ⚠ Trap: INCOSPAR was under the **DAE**, not the Department of Space.
[33:2:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T G2 Part 2 p.14-15 (INCOSPAR under Sarabhai, DoS under PM); PMF S&T Part 1 p.98; PMF S&T Part 2 p.30-31 (TERLS, ISRO 1969); app notes 5:33 (sub 0)
## SUB 3 | Key Milestones (1992-2026)
[33:3:0] TABLE head: Year | Milestone
  [33:3:0.0] 1992 | USA sanctioned ISRO for two years under the MTCR (cryogenic engine deal with Russia's Glavkosmos)
  [33:3:0.1] 1994 | PSLV-D2 (15 Oct 1994) – PSLV operational; placed IRS-P2 in a sun-synchronous orbit (UPSC 1995: "launching synchronous satellite")
  [33:3:0.2] 2008 | Chandrayaan-1 (22 Oct 2008, PSLV-C11): India's first Moon mission – the first Indian-built spacecraft to leave Earth's gravity
  [33:3:0.3] 2008 | Cabinet cleared Chandrayaan-2 (Indo-Russian plan then) at Rs 425 crore
  [33:3:0.4] 2014 | Mangalyaan: Mars orbit on maiden attempt; first Asian, India 4th country
  [33:3:0.5] 2017 | 104 satellites on one PSLV
  [33:3:0.6] 2019 | Mission Shakti (ASAT test); NSIL formed; Chandrayaan-2
  [33:3:0.7] 2023 | Chandrayaan-3: first landing near the lunar south pole; Aditya-L1 to the L1 point
  [33:3:0.8] 30 Dec 2024 / 16 Jan 2025 | SpaDeX launched on PSLV-C60 / docking done; India 4th (after US, Russia, China)
  [33:3:0.9] 24 Dec 2025 | LVM3-M6 lifts BlueBird Block-2 (6,100 kg), heaviest payload from Indian soil
  [33:3:0.10] 18 Jul 2026 | Skyroot's Vikram-1: first privately developed Indian rocket to reach orbit
[33:3:1] - **SpaDeX** = **Space Docking** technology demonstrator: two small spacecraft; not a Mars landing, space station or asteroid mining (APPSC DL 2023).
[33:3:2] - **Moon spacecraft name:** **Chandrayaan-I**; "Chang'e-1" (Change-I) is China's; "Antariksha" is a distractor.
[33:3:3] > India is 4th in both: Mars orbit (Mangalyaan) and space docking (SpaDeX).
[33:3:4] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.100-101 (PSLV-D2 1994, Chandrayaan-1 PSLV-C11, SSO); brahmand.com "Cabinet nod for Chandrayaan-II" (Rs 425 crore, fetched via search); app notes 5:33 (sub 2); general knowledge for the 1992 MTCR sanctions (not checked)

  [33:4:0.2] First human Moon landing | Apollo 11, July 1969 (Armstrong, Aldrin)

## SUB 5 | International Cooperation and Space Vision 2047
[33:5:0] TABLE head: Partner | Mission
  [33:5:0.0] USSR | Aryabhata, Bhaskara; Rakesh Sharma on Soyuz T-11 (3 Apr 1984) – first Indian in space
  [33:5:0.1] Indo-US | SITE with NASA (1975-76); NISAR launched 2025
  [33:5:0.2] Indo-French | APPLE on Ariane-1; Megha-Tropiques (2011); SARAL (2013)
  [33:5:0.3] ISRO-ESA | Ground-tracking support for Gaganyaan
  [33:5:0.4] Axiom-4 | Shubhanshu Shukla to the ISS, June-July 2025
[33:5:1] - **58th International Astronautical Congress:** **Hyderabad**, Sep 2007, hosted by ISRO; India's earlier IAC was Bangalore 1988.
[33:5:2] - **Vision 2047:** **Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035**; **Indian on the Moon by 2040**; next missions **Chandrayaan-4, Chandrayaan-5, Venus Orbiter Mission** (Rs **1,236 crore**).
[33:5:3] - **Gaganyaan:** crew of **3**, **400 km** orbit, **3 days**; splashdown in Indian waters.
[33:5:4] - Space economy: FDI up to **100%** in non-sensitive segments; IN-SPACe chairman **Pawan Kumar Goenka**.
[33:5:5] > ⚠ Trap: BAS target is **2035**, Moon landing **2040**; 2047 is only the Vision horizon.

=== NOTES 5:34 | Isro - Organisational Structure, Major Centres and Their Functions
## SUB 0 | ISRO Centres – Location and Function
[34:0:0] TABLE head: Centre | Full form | Location | Function
  [34:0:0.0] VSSC | Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre | Thiruvananthapuram (Kerala) | Lead centre, launch-vehicle design and development
  [34:0:0.1] LPSC | Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre | Valiamala (Kerala); Bengaluru unit – not Hyderabad | Liquid and cryogenic stages
  [34:0:0.2] IPRC | ISRO Propulsion Complex (earlier LPSC test facility) | Mahendragiri (Tamil Nadu, near Nagercoil) | Assembly and testing of liquid/cryogenic engines and stages; India's first cryogenic engine tests and the 2007 cryogenic test stand
  [34:0:0.3] SDSC-SHAR | Satish Dhawan Space Centre | Sriharikota (AP) | ISRO's main (only operational) launch centre
  [34:0:0.4] URSC | U R Rao Satellite Centre (earlier ISAC) | Bengaluru (Karnataka) | Satellite design and building
  [34:0:0.5] SAC | Space Applications Centre | Ahmedabad | Payloads (communication, remote sensing), applications research
  [34:0:0.6] NRSC | National Remote Sensing Centre (forerunner NRSA) | Hyderabad (Telangana) – not Delhi, Pune, Dehradun | Receiving, processing, distributing satellite data; a centre of ISRO under the Department of Space
  [34:0:0.7] HSFC | Human Space Flight Centre | Bengaluru (opened 30 Jan 2019) | Gaganyaan: mission planning, crew selection and training
  [34:0:0.8] MCF | Master Control Facility | Hassan (Karnataka, 1982); Bhopal (2005) | Control of geostationary satellites
  [34:0:0.9] ISTRAC | ISRO Telemetry, Tracking and Command Network | Bengaluru | Tracking launch vehicles and satellites
  [34:0:0.10] IIRS | Indian Institute of Remote Sensing | Dehradun (Uttarakhand) | Training (see IIRS page)
[34:0:1] - **Pairs (RAS 2018):** VSSC–Trivandrum ✓, URSC–Bengaluru ✓, NRSC–Dehradun ✗ (Hyderabad), IIRS–Hyderabad ✗ (Dehradun) → **A & B only**.
[34:0:2] > ⚠ Trap: IPRC Mahendragiri is in **Tamil Nadu**, not Kerala; NRSC = Hyderabad, IIRS = Dehradun (swapped in pair questions).
[34:0:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T G2 Part 2 p.9 (facilities list: LPSC Valiamala/Mahendragiri, NRSC Hyderabad, MCF Hassan, IIRS Dehradun); PMF S&T Part 2 p.31 (VSSC, URSC); app notes 5:34 (sub 3)
## SUB 1 | Sriharikota (SDSC-SHAR)
[34:1:0] # Location and history
[34:1:1] - **District:** **Nellore** when the APPSC 2019 papers were set; **Tirupati** district now (April 2022 reorganisation).
[34:1:2] - Barrier island between **Pulicat Lake (west)** and the **Bay of Bengal (east)**; it divides the lake from the sea (not Chilika, Mahanadi or Godavari mouth).
[34:1:3] - Set up **1971** as **Sriharikota High Altitude Range (SHAR)**; renamed **2002** after **Satish Dhawan**.
[34:1:4] - Why chosen: **east coast** (eastward launch gains from Earth's rotation), **near the equator**, **sea** for spent stages, **thinly populated**.
[34:1:5] # Facilities and launches
[34:1:6] TABLE head: Pad | Vehicles
  [34:1:6.0] First Launch Pad | PSLV, SSLV
  [34:1:6.1] Second Launch Pad | GSLV, LVM3; standby for PSLV
  [34:1:6.2] Third Launch Pad | For NGLV; approved 16 Jan 2025, Rs 3,984.86 crore, 48 months
[34:1:7] - **SPROB** (Solid Propellant Space Booster Plant): casts **S200** boosters of LVM3.
[34:1:8] - **Launch View Gallery:** opened **31 March 2019** (PSLV-C45); first phase seats **5,000** visitors.
[34:1:9] TABLE head: Launch | Mission | Date
  [34:1:9.0] ISRO's 100th space mission | PSLV-C21, from Sriharikota | Sept 2012
  [34:1:9.1] 100th launch from SHAR | GSLV-F15/NVS-02 | 29 Jan 2025
[34:1:10] - **February 2004:** blast at the solid propellant plant at SHAR, **Sriharikota**.
[34:1:11] # Second spaceport – Kulasekarapattinam
[34:1:12] - **SSLV Launch Complex**, **Thoothukudi** district, **Tamil Nadu** (approved 2023); **direct southward launch** to polar/sun-synchronous orbit, without the fuel-costly dog-leg around **Sri Lanka**.
[34:1:13] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 2 p.29-30 (SHAR 1971/2002, Pulicat, Kulasekarapattinam); Rocket AP Geography p.39 (SDSC SHAR, Sriharikota, Tirupati); Rocket Indian Geography p.99 (Sriharikota separates Pulicat from the Bay); isro.gov.in Launch View Gallery (via web search: 5,000 capacity); app notes 5:34 (sub 5)
## SUB 2 | IIRS and Training Bodies
[34:2:0] - **IIRS** (Indian Institute of Remote Sensing), **Dehradun** (not New Delhi, Lucknow, Nagpur); constituent unit of **ISRO, Department of Space**.
[34:2:1] - Founded **1966** as the **Indian Photo-interpretation Institute (IPI)** (not 1956, 1986, 1996).
[34:2:2] - Disciplines: **remote sensing, photogrammetry, cartography, geo-informatics/GIS** – **not angiography** (medical imaging).
[34:2:3] - Field equipment (tree caliper, electronic levelling instrument, snow density meter …) does **not** include a **LINAC** (linear accelerator).
[34:2:4] - **Director, Dec 2019:** **Dr Prakash Chauhan**.
[34:2:5] - **CSSTEAP**: Centre for Space Science and Technology Education in Asia and the Pacific; **UN-affiliated**; **1995**; hosted at IIRS Dehradun.
[34:2:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T G2 Part 2 p.4 (IIRS and CSSTEAP, Dehradun), p.9; app notes 5:34 (sub 8); general knowledge for the 2019 director (not checked)
## SUB 3 | Structure, Leadership and Commercial Arms
[34:3:0] - **ISRO** = **Indian Space Research Organisation**; under the **Department of Space**, which reports **directly to the Prime Minister**; HQ **Bengaluru**.
[34:3:1] - **ISRO Chairman** = also **Secretary, DoS** + **Chairman, Space Commission**; **Dr V. Narayanan** is the **11th** Chairman (from 14 Jan 2025), succeeding **S. Somanath**; **K. Sivan** took over on **15 Jan 2018** from A.S. Kiran Kumar; **M.G.K. Menon** was 2nd Chairman (1972).
[34:3:2] TABLE head: Body | Year | Role
  [34:3:2.0] Antrix Corporation | Sept 1992 | Commercial and marketing arm of ISRO (Miniratna 2008) – the answer, not "Devas" or "Antariksh"
  [34:3:2.1] NSIL (NewSpace India Ltd) | 2019 | CPSE, now the main commercial arm (PSLV-C53 was an NSIL mission)
  [34:3:2.2] IN-SPACe | 2020 | Single-window regulator, HQ Ahmedabad; chairman Pawan Kumar Goenka
  [34:3:2.3] Indian Space Policy | 2023 | –
[34:3:3] - India still has **no Space Activities Act** (2026).

## SUB 7 | Ground Network – ISTRAC
[34:7:0] - **ISTRAC** (HQ Bengaluru) runs the TTC network tracking launch vehicles through the ascent phase; stations abroad: **Mauritius, Brunei, Biak (Indonesia)**; **Indian Deep Space Network**: **Byalalu**, near Bengaluru.
[34:7:1] - **MoU, August 2017:** **ISTRAC/ISRO/Department of Space** with **CSIR-National Physical Laboratory (NPL)** – time and frequency traceability for ISRO's IRNWT timing stations (NavIC); valid 5 years.

=== NOTES 5:35 | Launch Vehicles - SLV-3, Aslv, Pslv, Gslv Mk-ii, LVM3, Sslv
## SUB 0 | Satellite to Launch Vehicle – Which Rocket Flew Which Mission
[35:0:0] # Missions most asked

  [35:0:1.0] Chandrayaan-1 | PSLV-C11 (XL) | Oct 2008
  [35:0:1.1] Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) | PSLV-C25 | Nov 2013 – not GSLV, not LVM3
  [35:0:1.2] Chandrayaan-2 | GSLV Mk III-M1 (LVM3-M1) | Jul 2019
  [35:0:1.3] Chandrayaan-3 | LVM3-M4 | 14 Jul 2023
  [35:0:1.4] Aditya-L1 | PSLV-C57 (XL) | 2 Sep 2023
  [35:0:1.5] 104 satellites (Cartosat-2 + 101 foreign) | PSLV-C37 | 15 Feb 2017 – multi-satellite record
  [35:0:1.6] METSAT (Kalpana-1) | PSLV-C4 | 12 Sep 2002 – first time PSLV put >1,000 kg (1,060 kg) towards geosynchronous orbit
  [35:0:1.7] INSAT-3DR (2,211 kg) | GSLV-F05 with indigenous cryogenic upper stage | Sep 2016
  [35:0:1.8] GSAT-19 | GSLV Mk III-D1 | 5 Jun 2017 – first operational LVM3
  [35:0:1.9] GISAT-1 | GSLV-F10 | Planned 5 Mar 2020, postponed; flew 12 Aug 2021, lost (cryogenic-stage anomaly)
  [35:0:1.10] TeLEOS-2 + Lumelite-4 (Singapore) | PSLV-C55 | 22 Apr 2023; 57th PSLV mission
  [35:0:1.11] NVS-01 | GSLV-F12 | May 2023
  [35:0:1.12] NVS-02 | GSLV-F15 | 29 Jan 2025; 100th launch from Sriharikota (17th GSLV flight); valve fault, not in intended orbit
  [35:0:1.13] OneWeb (36 satellites) | LVM3-M2 | 23 Oct 2022; M2 + M3 = 72 satellites
  [35:0:1.14] Sprites (world's smallest spacecraft, ~4 g chips) | PSLV-C38 | Jun 2017, on Venta-1 / Max Valier
  [35:0:1.15] SpaDeX | PSLV-C60 | 30 Dec 2024
  [35:0:1.16] RISAT-2BR1 + 9 foreign | PSLV-C48 | 11 Dec 2019; 50th PSLV flight
  [35:0:1.17] GSAT-6A | GSLV-F08 | Mar 2018; contact lost after launch
  [35:0:1.18] NISAR | GSLV-F16 | 30 Jul 2025; first GSLV to a sun-synchronous polar orbit
  [35:0:1.19] BlueBird Block-2 (AST SpaceMobile, USA) | LVM3-M6 | 24 Dec 2025; 6,100 kg – heaviest payload from Indian soil
  [35:0:1.20] EOS-05 | GSLV-F17 | 4 Sep 2026; India's first imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit
  [35:0:1.21] PSLV-C61/EOS-09 (18 May 2025) and PSLV-C62 (12 Jan 2026, 64th PSLV flight) | PSLV | Both failed at the third stage
[35:0:2] # LVM3-M2 / OneWeb India-1 (23 Oct 2022)
[35:0:3] - **Firsts:** **first commercial mission** of LVM3 and **first NSIL mission with LVM3**; first LVM3 launch to LEO; customer **Network Access Associates Ltd (OneWeb)**.
[35:0:4] - **Mass:** the **36 satellites together weighed 5,796 kg** (about 150 kg each) – the heaviest LVM3 payload then; the rocket itself weighs ~640 t.
[35:0:5] # Early record questions
[35:0:6] - **PSLV flight count:** PSLV-C14 (Oceansat-2, Sep 2009) was the **16th PSLV flight**; PSLV-C62 (Jan 2026) was the **64th**.
[35:0:7] - **CMS-01** went on **PSLV-C50**; 105th SHAR launch PSLV-C62; 107th GSLV-F17.
[35:0:8] > ⚠ Trap: Chandrayaan-1, MOM and Aditya-L1 = **PSLV**; Chandrayaan-2 and -3 = **LVM3**.
[35:0:9] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.100-101, p.135-136; PMF S&T Part 2 p.2, p.12-18; ISRO LVM3-M2/OneWeb India-1 page; app notes 5:35 sub 6-7
## SUB 1 | Stages, Configurations and Features – PSLV, GSLV, LVM3, SSLV
[35:1:0] # Configurations
[35:1:1] TABLE head: Vehicle | Full form | Stages
  [35:1:1.0] SLV-3 | Satellite Launch Vehicle-3 | 4, all-solid; 17 t, 22 m; 40 kg to LEO
  [35:1:1.1] ASLV | Augmented SLV | 5, all-solid; 40 t, 24 m; 150 kg to LEO
  [35:1:1.2] PSLV | Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle | 4: solid–liquid–solid–liquid (S139, Vikas, solid, twin-engine PS4); no cryogenic stage
  [35:1:1.3] GSLV Mk II | Geosynchronous SLV | 3: one solid + one earth-storable liquid (Vikas) + one cryogenic (CE-7.5) + 4 liquid strap-ons
  [35:1:1.4] LVM3 (ex-GSLV Mk III, "Bahubali") | Launch Vehicle Mark-3 | 3: 2 S200 solid strap-ons + L110 liquid core + C25 cryogenic (CE-20)
  [35:1:1.5] SSLV | Small SLV | 3 solid stages + liquid Velocity Trimming Module (VTM)
[35:1:2] - **PSLV:** **"workhorse" of ISRO**; third-generation vehicle; **first Indian vehicle with liquid stages**; ~1,750 kg to SSO; built to launch **IRS (earth-resources)** satellites into sun-synchronous polar orbit.
[35:1:3] - **PSLV variants:** CA (Core Alone) 0 strap-ons, DL 2, **QL 4**, XL 6 (extended).
[35:1:4] - **GSLV:** fourth-generation vehicle; first flight GSLV-D1 with **GSAT-1** (18 Apr 2001); 2–2.5 t communication / navigation satellites to **GTO**; launched **INSAT-3D/3DR, NVS** satellites.
[35:1:5] - **LVM3:** a **GSLV-class** vehicle (not built by DRDO); ~4 t to GTO, ~8 t to LEO; it launched **Chandrayaan-2 and -3**, **not** the Mars Orbiter Mission (PSLV).
[35:1:6] - **LVM3 – heaviest Indian rocket:** ~**640 t** lift-off mass, 43 m; first orbital flight **GSLV Mk III-D1** (5 Jun 2017, GSAT-19), called the ISRO "**game changer**" and India's "heavy rocket" of 2017; it ended dependence on foreign launchers for **4-tonne** satellites.
[35:1:7] - **LVM3 history:** **LVM3-X / CARE** suborbital test **18 Dec 2014**; operational since 2017.
[35:1:8] - **Not operational now:** **SLV-3 and ASLV** (retired); PSLV, GSLV, LVM3, SSLV and sounding rockets are in use.
[35:1:9] # SSLV
[35:1:10] - **Design:** **500 kg to 500 km LEO** (10–500 kg class; ~300 kg to SSO); **three solid stages** + VTM, ~**120 t** lift-off, **34 m** – shorter than PSLV and GSLV; low cost, **launch-on-demand**, minimal infrastructure; can be assembled **vertically and horizontally**.
[35:1:11] - **Flights:** **SSLV-D1** (Aug 2022) failed to place EOS-02 in orbit; **SSLV-D2 (10 Feb 2023)** – first successful SSLV launch; D3 (Aug 2024).
[35:1:12] - **HAL** won the **Rs 511 crore** Transfer of Technology to build SSLV – first full ToT of an ISRO launch vehicle.
[35:1:13] - **Second spaceport:** **Kulasekarapattinam** (Tamil Nadu) for SSLV, avoiding the dog-leg round Sri Lanka.
[35:1:14] > ⚠ Trap: "SSLV has two solid stages" is WRONG – it has three (APPSC G1); "GSLV Mk III is four-staged S-L-S-L" is WRONG – S-L-S-L is PSLV (UPSC 2018).
[35:1:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T G2 Part 2 p.7-8; PMF S&T Part 1 p.132-136; PMF S&T Part 2 p.1-6, p.11; ISRO SSLV page (sslv_CON); app notes 5:35 sub 2-3, 8
## SUB 2 | Chronology and Early Vehicles – SLV-3 and ASLV
[35:2:0] # Order of development
[35:2:1] - **Order:** **SLV-3 → ASLV → PSLV → GSLV → LVM3 → SSLV** (first flights 1979, 1987, 1993, 2001, 2014, 2022).
[35:2:2] TABLE head: Vehicle | First flight | First (successful) payload
  [35:2:2.0] SLV-3 | 10 Aug 1979 (E1, partly successful) | 18 Jul 1980 (E2): Rohini RS-1 – India the 6th nation to orbit a satellite with its own rocket
  [35:2:2.1] ASLV | 24 Mar 1987 (D1, failed; D2 1988 failed) | D3, 20 May 1992: SROSS-C; D4 1994: SROSS-C2
  [35:2:2.2] PSLV | 20 Sep 1993 (D1, failed) | 15 Oct 1994 (D2): IRS-P2
  [35:2:2.3] GSLV | 18 Apr 2001 (D1) | GSAT-1
  [35:2:2.4] LVM3 | 18 Dec 2014 (LVM3-X, suborbital) | CARE; 2017 D1: GSAT-19
  [35:2:2.5] SSLV | Aug 2022 (D1, failed) | D2, Feb 2023
[35:2:3] - **SLV-3:** project led by **A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**; Rohini launches 1980, 1981, 1983.
[35:2:4] - **Match:** SLV-3 – **Rohini**; ASLV – **SROSS-C**; PSLV – **Chandrayaan-1**; GSLV – **EDUSAT** (GSLV-F01, 2004).
[35:2:5] - **Mixed chronology:** Bangladesh formed **1971** → Pokhran-I **May 1974** → Sikkim the 22nd state **May 1975** → SLV-3 launch **1979/1980**.
[35:2:6] - **ISRO chronology:** LVM3-X **Dec 2014** → ASTROSAT **Sep 2015** → IRNSS-1I **Apr 2018**.
[35:2:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T G2 Part 2 p.4-7; PMF S&T Part 1 p.98-100, p.132-134; app notes 5:35 sub 1
## SUB 3 | Sounding Rockets and TERLS Thumba
[35:3:0] - **TERLS** (Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station), near **Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala** – **India's first rocket launching station**; chosen because the **geomagnetic (magnetic) equator** passes through it.
[35:3:1] - **First launch:** American **Nike-Apache**, **21 Nov 1963** – start of the Indian space programme; early imported rockets **M-100** (Russia) and **Centaure** (France).
[35:3:2] - **Rohini Sounding Rockets (RSR):** ISRO's own series (programme consolidated 1975); used for **atmospheric research** and to qualify sub-systems of launch vehicles; sub-orbital, ~70–600 km.
[35:3:3] TABLE head: Rocket | Fact
  [35:3:3.0] RH-200 | Two-stage, ~70–80 km, meteorology; 200th consecutive successful launch from Thumba, 23 Nov 2022
  [35:3:3.1] RH-300 Mk-II | Single-stage, ~116–160 km
  [35:3:3.2] RH-560 Mk-III | Two-stage, ~470–550 km, ionosphere
[35:3:4] - **Number = diameter in mm**; SLV, ASLV and PSLV are orbital launch vehicles, not sounding rockets.
[35:3:5] > Thumba = magnetic equator (sounding rockets); Sriharikota = east coast (orbital launches).
[35:3:6] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.98; PMF S&T Part 2 p.9-10; NextGen S&T G2 Part 2 p.6; app notes 5:35 sub 0
## SUB 4 | Orbits and Launch Physics
[35:4:0] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [35:4:0.0] LEO | Low Earth Orbit (up to ~2,000 km)
  [35:4:0.1] SSO | Sun-synchronous, near-polar; passes a place at the same local solar time – PSLV's speciality
  [35:4:0.2] GTO | Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit: elliptical, apogee near 36,000 km – GSLV, LVM3
  [35:4:0.3] GEO | Geostationary orbit over the equator; satellite appears fixed in the sky (reached via GSLV, not PSLV's polar orbits)
  [35:4:0.4] Apogee / perigee | Farthest / nearest point of an orbit
  [35:4:0.5] Strap-on booster | Extra motors fixed to the core for lift-off thrust
[35:4:1] - **Eastward launch:** satellites are launched **eastward** to use the Earth's **west-to-east rotation** (a free speed boost); sites **nearer the equator** gain most. The boost does **not** give "escape velocity" – an orbiting satellite never reaches escape velocity.
[35:4:2] - **Not always east:** polar / SSO launches go **southward** (from Sriharikota a **dog-leg around Sri Lanka**).
[35:4:3] - **Sriharikota** (SDSC-SHAR, Andhra Pradesh) on the **east coast**: rockets fly over the sea; all Indian orbital launches, incl. private ones, go from here.
[35:4:4] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 2 p.3; PMF S&T Part 1 p.64-66; app notes 5:35 sub 4
## SUB 5 | Private, Reusable and Future Vehicles
[35:5:0] TABLE head: Vehicle | Company | Fact
  [35:5:0.0] Vikram-S ("Prarambh") | Skyroot (Hyderabad) | 18 Nov 2022, Sriharikota; India's first private rocket (suborbital, 89.5 km)
  [35:5:0.1] Agnibaan SOrTeD | Agnikul Cosmos | 30 May 2024; 3D-printed Agnilet semi-cryogenic engine; India's first private launchpad at Sriharikota
  [35:5:0.2] Vikram-1 | Skyroot | 18 Jul 2026: first privately developed Indian rocket to reach orbit; Kalam-series solid stages
[35:5:1] - **PSLV by industry:** NSIL chose the **HAL–L&T consortium** to build **5 PSLV-XL** (2023) – end-to-end production by Indian industry.
[35:5:2] - **RLV = Reusable Launch Vehicle:** RLV-TD "Pushpak" landing tests (**RLV-LEX**, 2 Apr 2023; LEX-02, LEX-03 2024) at the **Aeronautical Test Range, Chitradurga, Karnataka** – a landing test, not an engine test.
[35:5:3] - **NGLV:** reusable-first-stage heavy launcher, **30 t to LEO** (Cabinet, 18 Sep 2024), for Bharatiya Antariksh Station (2035) and a **crewed lunar landing by 2040**.
[35:5:4] - **HLVM3:** human-rated LVM3 for **Gaganyaan** (crew to ~400 km for 3 days); first Integrated Air Drop Test **24 Aug 2025**.
[35:5:5] - **Foreign reusables:** **SpaceX Falcon 9** – first orbital-class booster landing **21 Dec 2015**; **Blue Origin New Shepard** – suborbital, landed Nov 2015.
[35:5:6] - **FDI:** **49% automatic** FDI in launch vehicles and spaceports.
[35:5:7] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 2 p.6-9; NextGen S&T G2 Part 2 p.34; IANS report of Cabinet decision (18 Sep 2024); app notes 5:35 sub 9-10
## SUB 6 | Cryogenic Stages of the Launch Vehicles
[35:6:0] - **Early GSLVs** flew **Russian KVD-1** cryogenic stages; technology transfer was refused in the 1990s, so India built its own. **First indigenous cryogenic success: GSLV-D5 (Jan 2014)** – not GSLV-D1 (2001).
[35:6:1] TABLE head: Engine / type | Propellant | Used in
  [35:6:1.0] CE-7.5 (cryogenic) | LH2 + LOX | GSLV Mk II upper stage
  [35:6:1.1] CE-20 (cryogenic) | LH2 + LOX | C25 stage of LVM3
  [35:6:1.2] SCE-200 / SE2000 (semi-cryogenic) | Refined kerosene + LOX | LVM3 upgrade, NGLV
  [35:6:1.3] Vikas (earth-storable) | UH25 + N2O4 | PSLV 2nd, GSLV 2nd stage
  [35:6:1.4] Solid | HTPB | GSLV 1st stage
[35:6:2] - **"CE-25 / C25" news (2017):** the **C25** cryogenic upper stage with the CE-20, India's first high-thrust indigenous cryogenic engine, was ground-tested for **GSLV Mk III**.
[35:6:3] - **Engine testing:** **IPRC Mahendragiri (Tamil Nadu)**; LPSC Valiamala does design.
[35:6:4] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.136-137; PMF S&T Part 2 p.1-2; app notes 5:35 sub 5

=== NOTES 5:37 | Communication Satellites – Insat and Gsat Series
## SUB 0 | INSAT System
[37:0:0] # Firsts
[37:0:1] TABLE head: Year | Milestone
  [37:0:1.0] 19 Jun 1981 | APPLE (Ariane Passenger PayLoad Experiment) – first experimental geostationary comsat, on Ariane-1 from Kourou, French Guiana
  [37:0:1.1] 1982 | INSAT-1A – first INSAT (INSAT-1 series built abroad by Ford Aerospace)
  [37:0:1.2] 1983 | INSAT system commissioned; INSAT-1B made it operational
  [37:0:1.3] 1990 | INSAT-1D – linked India by TV from ~36,000 km
  [37:0:1.4] 10 Jul 1992 | INSAT-2A, Kourou – first of the fully indigenous INSAT-2 series
  [37:0:1.5] 12 Sep 2002 | METSAT (PSLV-C4), renamed KALPANA-1 after Kalpana Chawla – India's first exclusive weather satellite
[37:0:2] # Design and management
[37:0:3] - **INSAT = Indian National Satellite** system: **multipurpose** geostationary system – telecom, TV, **meteorology**, disaster warning, search-and-rescue, tele-education, telemedicine (**not astronomy**); asked as "**Meteorological Satellite**" (not resource, military or polar).
[37:0:4] - Joint venture of **DoS, DoT, IMD, AIR, Doordarshan**; coordinated by **ICC**; **Master Control Facility, Hassan** (Karnataka).
[37:0:5] - **Cyclones** are tracked through **INSAT** (INSAT-3D/3DR imagers); INSAT-3D and 3DR sharply cut cyclone deaths on the east coast, incl. AP. **INSAT-1C** (1988) has no disaster-management role; RISAT-2B, INSAT-3D, INSAT-3DR do.
[37:0:6] # Key INSATs
[37:0:7] TABLE head: Satellite | Launch | Note
  [37:0:7.0] INSAT-3C | Jan 2002, Ariane-4, Kourou | Communication
  [37:0:7.1] INSAT-3A | 10 Apr 2003, Kourou | Multipurpose – broadcasting, mobile, meteorology
  [37:0:7.2] INSAT-3E | Sep 2003, Kourou (French Guiana) | Communication
  [37:0:7.3] INSAT-4A | 22 Dec 2005, Ariane-5, Kourou | First of INSAT-4 (3,081 kg)
  [37:0:7.4] INSAT-4C | 10 Jul 2006, GSLV-F02 – exploded 60 s after lift-off | 2,168 kg; replaced by INSAT-4CR (Sep 2007, GSLV-F04)
[37:0:8] - **Launched abroad:** till 2002 **all INSATs** went up from abroad (USA, Kourou); later INSAT-4CR, INSAT-3DR, INSAT-3DS flew on GSLV from Sriharikota.
[37:0:9] - **Launch sites:** **Kourou** (French Guiana, Ariane – Europe's spaceport); **Cape Canaveral** on the Atlantic coast of **Florida** (US); Baikonur (Kazakhstan, Russia).
[37:0:10] - **NSIL** took 10 in-orbit comsats (2022); **19** operational comsats (2026).
[37:0:11] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.98-103, p.106; NextGen S&T G2 Part 2 p.12; app notes 5:37 sub 1
## SUB 1 | GSAT Series – Key Satellites
[37:1:0] TABLE head: Satellite | Launch | Note
  [37:1:0.0] GSAT-1 | 2001, GSLV-D1, Sriharikota | Experimental; digital broadcast and internet payloads
  [37:1:0.1] GSAT-3 (EDUSAT) | 2004, GSLV-F01 | World's first dedicated educational satellite – links schools
  [37:1:0.2] GSAT-8 | 21 May 2011, Ariane-5 VA-202, Kourou | DTH; GAGAN payload (also GSAT-10, -15)
  [37:1:0.3] GSAT-10 | 29 Sep 2012, Ariane-5 | Heaviest Indian comsat at that time
  [37:1:0.4] GSAT-6 | 2015 | 25th Indian GEO comsat (ISRO-built, not DRDO); large deployable antenna, S-band
  [37:1:0.5] GSAT-18 | 6 Oct 2016, Ariane-5 VA-231, Kourou | 3,404 kg – the comsat of October 2016
  [37:1:0.6] GSAT-19 | 5 Jun 2017, GSLV Mk III-D1 | 3,136 kg – heaviest satellite launched by India then; high-throughput
  [37:1:0.7] GSAT-11 | Dec 2018, French Guiana | Heaviest ISRO-built (~5.8 t), HTS, BharatNet
  [37:1:0.8] GSAT-31 | 6 Feb 2019, Ariane-5, Kourou | DTH, VSAT links for ATMs, stock exchanges, e-governance
  [37:1:0.9] GSAT-30 | 17 Jan 2020, Ariane-5 VA-251, Kourou | Telecommunication, C and Ku bands; to GTO, not a Sun-synchronous orbit
  [37:1:0.10] GSAT-24 | 23 Jun 2022, Ariane-5, Kourou | 4,180 kg, 24 Ku-band transponders; NSIL's first demand-driven mission (Tata Play)
  [37:1:0.11] CMS-01 | PSLV-C50, Sriharikota | Communication
  [37:1:0.12] GSAT-N2 (GSAT-20) | Nov 2024, SpaceX Falcon 9, Cape Canaveral | Ka-band broadband
  [37:1:0.13] CMS-03 (GSAT-7R) | 2 Nov 2025, LVM3-M5 | 4,410 kg – heaviest comsat from Indian soil; Navy
[37:1:1] - **Other astronomy facts:** **ASTROSAT** (2015) = India's first dedicated astronomy satellite; **Kepler** is NASA's, not ISRO's.
[37:1:2] - **Hughes Communications India** launched India's first **High-Throughput Satellite (HTS) broadband** service with ISRO's GSAT-11 and GSAT-29 capacity (2022).
[37:1:3] - **China:** **Shijian-20**, its heaviest satellite, went up on **Long March 5** (Dec 2019).
[37:1:4] > GSAT-11 = heaviest ISRO-built; CMS-03 = heaviest comsat launched from Indian soil; GSAT-19 = heaviest launched by India in 2017.
[37:1:5] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.103-106; ISRO GSAT-8 and GSAT-18 pages; app notes 5:37 sub 2-3; general knowledge (Hughes HTS, Shijian-20)
## SUB 2 | Geostationary Orbit – Physics of a Communication Satellite
[37:2:0] TABLE head: Orbit | Fact
  [37:2:0.0] Low Earth | 160–2,000 km; ISS ~400 km
  [37:2:0.1] Geostationary (GEO) | About 36,000 km (35,786 km) above the equator = orbit radius ~42,000 km (42,164 km from Earth's centre); period 24 hours (1 day)
  [37:2:0.2] Polar | Passes over the poles
  [37:2:0.3] Elliptical | Apogee and perigee differ
  [37:2:0.4] Circular | Centripetal force equals gravitational force
[37:2:1] - **Geostationary:** revolves **in the same direction as the Earth rotates** (west to east) with the same period, so it appears fixed over one point; it stays at a **fixed height** that does **not depend on its mass**.
[37:2:2] - **What keeps it in orbit:** the **centripetal force**, supplied by the **Earth's gravitational pull on the satellite** – not a rocket engine, not the Sun.
[37:2:3] - **No energy needed** to keep orbiting: in near-vacuum there is no drag; solar panels only power the instruments.
[37:2:4] - **Global TV:** **geostationary satellites** relay TV across the world (three cover nearly the whole globe); ground and space waves are short-range.
[37:2:5] - **Uplink / downlink:** sending data **up to the satellite / network** = **uplink**; receiving from it = downlink.
[37:2:6] - Launcher → elliptical **GTO** → satellite's own motor raises it to GEO.
[37:2:7] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.64-66; app notes 5:37 sub 0
## SUB 3 | Strategic and Regional Satellites
[37:3:0] TABLE head: Satellite | User
  [37:3:0.0] GSAT-7 "Rukmini" (INSAT-4F), 30 Aug 2013, Ariane-5 | Navy – exclusively military communication; replaced by CMS-03
  [37:3:0.1] GSAT-7A "Angry Bird" (2018) | Air Force
  [37:3:0.2] GSAT-7B (proposed) | Army
[37:3:1] - CMS-03: encrypted anti-jam naval links to **2,000 km** offshore.
[37:3:2] - **South Asia Satellite = GSAT-9**, GSLV-F09, **5 May 2017**; for **Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Sri Lanka**; **Pakistan opted out**.
[37:3:3] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.104-105; app notes 5:37 sub 4
## SUB 4 | Transponder Bands and Applications
[37:4:0] TABLE head: Band | Use
  [37:4:0.0] C / extended C | Telecom, TV distribution
  [37:4:0.1] Ku | DTH, VSAT
  [37:4:0.2] Ka | High-throughput broadband (GSAT-11, GSAT-N2)
  [37:4:0.3] S | Mobile satellite services, DWS downlink
[37:4:1] - **MF band is NOT used**. High-throughput: GSAT-19, -29, -11, N2; support **BharatNet**.
[37:4:2] - **DTH**, **VSAT**, **DSNG** (news gathering), **MSS** (mobile satellite services), GRAMSAT, telemedicine.
[37:4:3] - **Swayam Prabha**: **GSAT-15**, 40 free DTH education channels.
[37:4:4] - **DWS**: Cyclone Warning Centre **Chennai**; uplink **C**, downlink **S** to addressable coastal receivers.
[37:4:5] - Search and rescue: **COSPAS-SARSAT**.
[37:4:6] - **AP**: SDSC-SHAR gives APSDMA cyclone-track data; RTGS–SHAR MoU (**Jun 2025**); **satellite phones** in emergencies; the AP government signed an MoU with **Malaysia** (MEASAT Satellite Systems) for **Ku-band** services on **MEASAT-1 and MEASAT-2**.
[37:4:7] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.103-105; app notes 5:37 sub 5-6; general knowledge (MEASAT MoU)

=== NOTES 5:38 | Navigation Satellites – Irnss/navic and Gagan
## SUB 0 | Satellite Navigation Systems of the World – Owners and Full Forms
[38:0:0] # Four global, two regional systems
[38:0:1] TABLE head: System | Owner | Scope
  [38:0:1.0] GPS – Global Positioning System | USA (Dept of Defense) | Global
  [38:0:1.1] GLONASS | Russia (not the UK) | Global
  [38:0:1.2] Galileo | European Union (not the USA) – live 2016, under civilian control, works with GPS and GLONASS | Global
  [38:0:1.3] BeiDou | China | Global
  [38:0:1.4] NavIC (formerly IRNSS) | India | Regional
  [38:0:1.5] QZSS (Michibiki) | Japan | Regional
[38:0:2] - **Which country has its own system?** Among Australia, Canada, Israel, Japan only **Japan** (QZSS) does (UPSC 2023).
[38:0:3] - **Galileo Project** (UPSC 2007): Europe's **multi-satellite navigation** project, not a missile shield.
[38:0:4] # GPS basics
[38:0:5] - **GPS** programme begun **1973**, first satellite 1978, fully operational 1995.
[38:0:6] - Original design: **24 satellites in 6 orbits** at about **20,200 km** (MEO); each circles Earth **twice a day**; about 30 in use (2026).
[38:0:7] - Signals in **L1** and **L2** bands; a **1 microsecond** clock error ≈ **300 m** position error.
[38:0:8] - A receiver needs **4 satellites**: 3 for position, 1 to correct its own clock error (trilateration).
[38:0:9] > Exam angle: "wrong pair" items swap owners – GLONASS–UK and Galileo–USA are the traps (APPSC 2018, 2019).
[38:0:10] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.113-117; UPSC 2023 key; app notes 5:38 sub 0
## SUB 1 | NavIC (IRNSS) – Constellation, Coverage and Services
[38:1:0] # Names and genesis
[38:1:1] - **IRNSS = Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System**; operational name **NavIC = Navigation with Indian Constellation**, given by PM **Narendra Modi** (2016).
[38:1:2] - Genesis: the US denied GPS data to India in the **1999 Kargil War** (**Operation Vijay**).
[38:1:3] - NavIC is **independent** of GPS: it keeps its own **Indian time** (IRNSS Network Time, from on-board atomic clocks), not GPS time.
[38:1:4] - Providing PNT since **2018**; India is the **only developing country** with its own independent regional system.
[38:1:5] # Constellation and coverage
[38:1:6] - **7 satellites: 3 GEO + 4 inclined GSO** (at **29°**), about 36,000 km up – not 4 GEO + 3 GSO, not 12.
[38:1:7] - Covers India and **about 1,500 km** beyond its borders (not "5,500 sq km"); **regional, not global** (UPSC 2018: only statement 1 correct).
[38:1:8] - Signals in **L5 and S bands**; the new **NVS** satellites add a civilian **L1** signal.
[38:1:9] TABLE head: Service | Users | Accuracy
  [38:1:9.0] Standard Positioning Service (SPS) | All civilians (open) | Better than 20 m (about 5 m in practice)
  [38:1:9.1] Restricted Service (RS) | Military / authorised | Encrypted
[38:1:10] - Nodal body for NavIC and GAGAN: **Satellite Navigation Programme Office**, ISRO.
[38:1:11] > Exam angle: IRNSS ≠ GAGAN – a statement "IRNSS is also known as GAGAN" is false.
[38:1:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 2 p.6; PMF S&T Part 1 p.113-118; testbook TSPSC HWO 2018 key (Indian clock)
## SUB 2 | IRNSS and NVS Satellites – Launches and Atomic Clocks
[38:2:0] # Launches
[38:2:1] - **IRNSS-1A**, India's first dedicated navigation satellite: **PSLV-C22**, **1 July 2013**, **Sriharikota**; the whole IRNSS-1 series flew on **PSLV**.
[38:2:2] - **11** navigation satellites launched since 2013, all from Sriharikota.
[38:2:3] TABLE head: Satellite | Vehicle / date | Note
  [38:2:3.0] NVS-01 (2nd generation) | GSLV-F12, May 2023 | First indigenous rubidium clock
  [38:2:3.1] NVS-02 | GSLV-F15, 29 Jan 2025 | 100th Sriharikota launch; valve (pyro connector) glitch → wrong orbit
[38:2:4] # Atomic clocks
[38:2:5] - **Caesium** clock is the world's **standard of time** (the SI second); NavIC satellites carry **rubidium** clocks (three each), smaller but slightly less accurate.
[38:2:6] - First-generation rubidium clocks from Swiss firm **SpectraTime** failed → indigenous clocks by **SAC, Ahmedabad**.
[38:2:7] - **13 Mar 2026:** last clock on **IRNSS-1F** stopped → only **3** PNT satellites (1B, 1I, NVS-01), below the **4** needed for a fix.
[38:2:8] # Limitations
[38:2:9] - **Regional** coverage only; thin **receiver** ecosystem (L5/S rarely in phone chips; L1 on NVS helps); clock failures + NVS-02 failure → NavIC could not fully replace GPS (Mar 2026).
[38:2:10] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.114; Uttarakhand PCS 2012 explanation (PSLV-C22); app notes 5:38 sub 2, 5
## SUB 3 | Uses of GPS and NavIC; Space Weather
[38:3:0] # Applications
[38:3:1] - **GPS / satellite timing** is used in **mobile phone networks, banking and power grids** – all three (UPSC 2018).
[38:3:2] - **Tectonic plate movement** is monitored with **GPS** (with VLBI and SLR) – not GIS or weather radar.
[38:3:3] - NavIC: terrestrial, aerial, marine navigation; **disaster management**; vehicle tracking and **fleet management**; precise timing (IST, power, telecom, banking); mapping and geodesy; **precision farming**; hikers and drivers.
[38:3:4] - **MoRTH AIS-140:** NavIC/GPS trackers and panic buttons compulsory in **public transport and commercial vehicles** (not all private cars).
[38:3:5] - **Qualcomm Snapdragon** chipsets support NavIC; reconfigured **IRNSS-1A** and GEMINI devices send cyclone, tsunami and high-wave alerts to **fishermen**.
[38:3:6] - **Elena Geo Systems:** India's **first NavIC-based device**, for precise directions on infrastructure projects (APPSC 2023).
[38:3:7] - **Himachal Pradesh** made a **GPS device mandatory for trekkers** (June 2019).
[38:3:8] - **APSDMA** uses **Satellite Based Mobile Data Voice (SBMDV)** terminals for real-time satellite communication (IRNSS, NavIC, SBAS are navigation, not communication).
[38:3:9] - Strategic autonomy: forces need not depend on foreign systems in a conflict.
[38:3:10] # Solar storms
[38:3:11] - A major **solar storm** can make **GPS fail**, damage **power grids**, cause **auroras** far from the poles, disturb **satellite orbits** and cut **shortwave radio** on polar flights – not tsunamis or forest fires (UPSC 2022).
[38:3:12] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.115-116; NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 2 p.6; gktoday / Business Standard (HP trekkers, 2019); UPSC 2018, 2022 keys
## SUB 4 | GAGAN and Other Satellite-Based Augmentation Systems
[38:4:0] - **GAGAN = GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation**: India's **SBAS**, built jointly by **ISRO + Airports Authority of India** (not DRDO); operational since **2015** (DGCA-certified).
[38:4:1] - Not an independent system: ground reference stations compute live corrections for orbit, clock and **ionospheric delay**, sent via **GEO** satellites → more **accuracy and integrity**.
[38:4:2] - Payloads on **GSAT-8, GSAT-10, GSAT-15**; covers the **Indian Flight Information Region**; precision-like approach (APV-I) without ILS.
[38:4:3] - Benefits go **beyond aviation** – maritime (GEMINI), railways, roads, survey, disaster response – so "only aviation" is false (UPSC 2025: I and II only).
[38:4:4] - GAGAN is one of the systems ISRO uses for **satellite navigation services** (INSAT, IRS, AstroSat are not).
[38:4:5] TABLE head: SBAS | Region
  [38:4:5.0] WAAS | USA
  [38:4:5.1] EGNOS | Europe
  [38:4:5.2] MSAS | Japan
  [38:4:5.3] GAGAN | India
[38:4:6] > Exam angle: GAGAN augments GPS for aviation; NavIC is an independent regional system.
[38:4:7] ~~ Sources: PMF S&T Part 1 p.118-125 (UPSC 2025 explanation)
